unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Ignited by heat and open flame. Burning releases hydrochloric acid fumes. Containers may explode in fire because of polymerization.
symptoms: Eye, nose, and throat irritation; headaches, nausea, vomiting.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical attention as soon as possible.
stability: Unavailable
incompatibility: Dissolves most paints, causes rubber to swell. The wet product will pit carbon steel.
hazardous_polymerization: Containers may explode in fire because of polymerization.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Evacuate personnel not equipped with protective clothing and respiratory protection. Shut off all ignition sources. Flush area with water spray. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * PEL and TLV based upon Epichlorohydrin. + Unavailable
general_note: *Vapor extremely irritating. Lung injury may be delayed. Liquid causes severe burns. Absorbed by leather and causes delayed burns. NOTE: Related cargo, epichlorohydrin, is a suspected carcinogen.

synonyms: 1-Chloro-2-nitrobenzene; 2-Chloro-1-nitrobenzene; Chloronitrobenzenes; o-Nitrochlorobenzene
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water spray, CO2, dry chemical, foam
special_fire_procedures: Water or foam may cause frothing. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus, eye protection and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight hazard when exposed to heat or flame. Toxic vapors of nitric oxides (NOx), hydrogen chloride (HCl), and carbon dioxide (CO2) are given off by high temperatures or combustion.
symptoms: Headache, weakness, anemia, shallow respiration, convulsions, coma, cyanosis.
short_term_exposure: 2 mg/m3. The effects of this poison are cumulative.
first_aid: Remove from exposure. If indicated give artificial respiration. Flush eyes with large amounts of water for at least 15 minutes. Wash skin with soap and water. If swallowed, give emetic, gastric lavage.
stability: Stable. Toxic vapors of NO2, HCl, CO2 are given off by high temperatures of combustion. Reacts with caustics.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Soak up with a mixture of sand and soda ash (9:1). Scoop up and place in cartons and burn. Wear butyl rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing and safety shoes. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Shipped in the molten state at 40°C. + Unavailable
general_note: Very toxic via inhalation, ingestion. Possibility of thermal burns from hot liquid. The molten liquid is irritating to the skin. Class B poison.

synonyms: Chlorosulfuric acid; Chlorsulfonic acid; Chlorsulfuric acid; Sulfuric chlorohydrin
appearance: Colorless to light liquid; pungent odor
electrical_group: B (based upon possible hydrogen gas (H2) generation should a leak or spill occur)
fire_extinguishing_agent: Non-flammable.
special_fire_procedures: DO NOT USE WATER. Wear full protective clothing, including self-contained breathing apparatus. Cool adjacent tanks with water spray from a distance.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Non-flammable, but it may cause ignition by contact with combustible materials. Dangerously reactive. Explosive concentrations of hydrogen gas can accumulate inside metal tanks containing this acid. Spill in confined space may produce explosive concentration of hydrogen. See data sheet for hydrogen.
symptoms: Contact of liquid with the skin can cause severe burns. Breathing the vapors will cause severe irritation and watering of the eyes.
short_term_exposure: 30 ppm for 10 minutes; 10 ppm for 60 minutes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Oxygen, administered by trained personnel, is often helpful. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Violently reacts with water forming sulfuric and hydrochloric acids.
incompatibility: Dangerously reactive. In addition to attacking many metals, the acid is a strong oxidizing agent and will react with water and organic materials with evolution of heat and large quantities of dense fumes.
cargo_group: Chlorosulfonic acid is unassigned in the compatibility chart. For compatibility assistance, call G-MTH-1 (202-267-1577).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with spilled liquid. From a distance carefully flush the spill away with water. Great care must be taken as water and chlorosulfonic acid react violently forming toxic HCl fumes and sulfuric acid. Consequently, clean-up personnel should work with the wind at their backs. If water is not available or if inversion conditions prevail, apply dry sand, vermiculite ashes or powdered clay to absorb the spill. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * Reacts violently forming hydrochloric and sulfuric acids.
general_note: Vapor inhalation may cause loss of consciousness with serious damage to lung tissue. Liquid causes severe irritation and watering of the eyes.
extraction_note: Boiling point, freezing point, vapor pressure, vapor density, and water solubility values were entirely absent from the text layer for this page.

synonyms: Coal tar distillate; Crude coal tar; High temperature coal tar; Tar; Tar, liquid
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water spray, foam, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Wear full protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus. Remove containers from fire if possible; if not possible, cool containers with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when heated.
symptoms: Inhalation: headache, nausea, vomiting; irritation to respiratory tract. Skin contact: highly irritating, dermatitis; sensitizes skin to light. Eyes: vapor exposure irritating. Ingestion: vapor toxic, vomiting, mild convulsions, hypothermia, dizziness
short_term_exposure: Keep exposures below the TLV/TWA of 0.2 mg/m3.
long_term_exposure: Prolonged exposure causes cancer in animals. Known carcinogen.
first_aid: Eye contact: flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Skin contact: remove contaminated clothing, wash affected areas with soap and water. Inhalation: remove to fresh air. Oxygen or artificial respiration as needed. Ingestion: induce vomiting, give oxygen if respiration shallow; swallow activated charcoal.
stability: Stable. Incompatible with strong oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Swells and softens rubber.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus. Remove all ignition sources. Ventilate spill area if enclosed. Collect spilled liquid for proper disposition. Use absorbants for small spills; dike spill area for large spills. After spill removal, wash down spill site. Material is a serious pollution hazard. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Prolonged exposure causes cancer in animals. Known carcinogen.

unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flammable, moderate fire risk.

first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing is difficult, administer oxygen. If breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—flush affected areas for 15 minutes with water. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Compatible with steel; certain rubbers and plastics are incompatible.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, plastic coated protective clothing. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus. Approach from up-wind side. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Small spills may be flushed away with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Main hazard is vapor inhalation.

fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, foam, or carbon dioxide.

unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.

incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.

special_fire_procedures: Provide fire fighters with breathing apparatus. Water or foam may cause frothing. Do not direct water directly into a fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.

stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Not corrosive to iron or steel.

general_note: Severe neurological disturbances when fumes are inhaled at high concentrations. Moderately toxic, skin and eye irritant.

synonyms: Cresol (2-, 3-, 4-); Cresylic acid; Cresylol; Hydroxymethyl benzene; Hydroxytoluene; Methylphenol (2-, 3-, or 4-); Oxytoluenes; Tar acids; Toluol (o-, m-, p-); Tricresol

general_note: Suspected carcinogens. Causes severe burns. Poisonous by skin absorption. Odor threshold is about the same as the TLV. Exposure to potentially dangerous vapor concentration can occur before the product can be detected by smell.

Add small amount of water and mix. Scoop up. Wash site with soap solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Vapor extremely irritating. Liquid causes severe burns. A lachrymator.

incompatibility: Compatible with aluminum, steel, stainless steel; not compatible with galvanized iron.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Cover spill with sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3). Add small amount of water and mix. Scoop up. Wash site with soap solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor irritating to mucous membranes.

synonyms: Acrylic acid, isodecyl ester; Isodecyl acrylate; Isodecyl propenoate
fire_extinguishing_agent: Foam, dry chemical, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Water might be ineffective. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: May polymerize to gummy solid. Reaction is not violent.
symptoms: Skin contact: Swelling and redness.
short_term_exposure: 8 hour exposure of rats to concentrated vapors approaching saturation in air was not fatal. Inhalation causes mild irritation of nose and throat; vapor mildly irritates eyes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air. Give artificial respiration if breathing stops. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable if inhibited.
incompatibility: Will swell and soften certain rubbers and soften and remove certain paints.
hazardous_polymerization: Stable if inhibited; can polymerize to a gummy solid.
spill_or_leak_procedure: If possible wear rubber gloves, face shield, and protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. Flush away with water. Do not flush into confined space (such as a sewer) because of the danger of explosion. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid causes swelling and redness after about 10 minutes.

synonyms: Alcohol C-10; Capric alcohol; 1-Decanol; Nonylcarbinol
appearance: Colorless, water white liquid; sour odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, carbon dioxide, dry chemical, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Not pertinent
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame; can react with oxidizing materials.
symptoms: Skin and eye contact—considerable pain and irritation to eyes; skin irritation.
first_aid: Eye contact—flood gently with clean water for at least 15 minutes. Skin contact—remove contaminated clothing and wash affected areas with plenty of water.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Mild steel is suitable for tanks, pipes, valves.
cargo_group: Group 20 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Practically non-toxic. Handle as a detergent. Main hazard is liquid contact with eyes.

synonyms: Diacetone; 4-Hydroxy-4-methyl-2-pentone; 4-Hydroxy-4-methyl pentanone-2; 2-Methyl-2-pentanol-4-one
appearance: Colorless to light yellow liquid; faint, pleasant odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, water fog, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Fire parties should be provided with respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Burning of eyes and nasal passages; dizziness, drowsiness.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Relatively stable. Can react with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Dissolves or softens many plastics.
cargo_group: Group 20 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Irritating to eyes and mucous membranes. Narcotic in high concentration. Experimentally has caused anemia and damage to kidneys and liver.

synonyms: 1-Butanamine, N-butyl-; N-Butyl-1-butanamine; di-n-butylamine; n-Dibutylamine; di-(n-butyl)amine
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined space—CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Use water to cool fire exposed containers. Water may be ineffective on fire. Wear goggles and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Toxic oxides of nitrogen may form in fires. Flammable, moderate fire risk.
symptoms: Watering, redness, or burning of eyes, irritation of skin, irritation of mucous membranes.
first_aid: In case of contact with eyes and skin, immediately flush with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes. For eyes get medical attention. Remove contaminated clothing and shoes at once. Call a doctor.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Carbon steel, cast iron, aluminum, stainless steel, phenolic-lined steel, nickel or tinned iron are suitable materials of construction. Do not use copper or copper alloys.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, face-shield, all-purpose canister respirator, protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Cover with sodium bisulfate and clean up. Flush spill with large quantities of water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Irritation of eyes and respiratory tracts, severe to eyes and moderate to skin after contact of short period of exposure.

synonyms: No common synonyms.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined space: CO2, dry chemical.
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous fire risk.
symptoms: Irritation of eyes, skin, and mucous membranes.
first_aid: Flush eyes and skin with water for 15 minutes. Remove contaminated clothing and flush underlying area with water. Call a doctor as soon as possible.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Carbon steel, aluminum, stainless steel, nickel, tinned iron, and phenolic-lined steel are suitable materials of construction. Do not use copper or copper alloys, zinc, or galvanized steel.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, face-shield or all-purpose canister respirator, protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Cover with sodium bisulfate and clean up. Flush spill with large quantities of water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Irritation of eyes and respiratory tracts, severe to eyes moderate to skin after contact of short period of time.

synonyms: Benzene, 1,2-dichloro-; 1,2-Dichlorobenzene; o-Dichlorobenzol; Dowtherm E; Orthodichlorobenzene
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water spray, dry chemical, CO2, foam.
special_fire_procedures: Wear full protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous. When heated to decomposition, emits highly toxic chloride fumes.
symptoms: Drowsiness, unsteadiness, eye irritation, difficulty in breathing.
short_term_exposure: Painful to some at 60-100 ppm for more than a few minutes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Most rubbers are not compatible.
spill_or_leak_procedure: If possible, wear butyl rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. If possible, absorb or mix with vermiculite, sodium bicarbonate or sand. This may be packaged in cardboard cartons and burned in an open pit. Wash site thoroughly with strong soap solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor inhalation causes moderate local irritation of nose and airway.

synonyms: Difluorodichloromethane; F 12; Freon 12; Halon 122; Methane, dichlorodifluoro-; Propellant 12; Refrigerant 12; Ucon 12
fire_extinguishing_agent: None
special_fire_procedures: When heated to decomposition temperature, it emits highly toxic fumes of phosgene and fluorides. Fire fighters must wear self-contained breathing apparatus and full protective clothing. Cool tanks exposed to fire with continuous water spray.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Does not burn. Toxic fumes emitted when heated to decomposition.
symptoms: Drowsiness with or without nausea.
short_term_exposure: Human exposure to 100,000 ppm for a few minutes produces unconsciousness.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air; if he stops breathing, apply artificial respiration. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Noncorrosive.
hazardous_decomposition_products: Phosgene and fluorides (on heating to decomposition).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid may cause skin or eye injury similar to frostbite. Vapor not toxic but breathing it may cause unconsciousness without warning because of lack of oxygen.

synonyms: Asymmetrical Dichloroethane; Chlorinated hydrochloric ether; Ethane, 1,1-dichloro-; Ethylidene chloride; Ethylidene dichloride; 1,1-Ethylidene dichloride
appearance: Colorless oily liquid; chloroform-like ethereal odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, foam, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire. Keep exposed tanks cool with water spray. Provide fire fighters with protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: When heated, toxic and highly flammable vapors are given off.
symptoms: Vapor causes eye irritation, dizziness, intoxication. Liquid causes slight irritation.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air, if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—flush areas immediately with water for 15 minutes.
stability: Generally stable, but decomposes when heated forming toxic and flammable vapors. Incompatible with strong oxidizers and caustics.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear protective clothing, face shield, goggles, respiratory protection. Secure ignition sources. Water spray may be used to flush spills away. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: This compound is a teratogen; 1,2-Dichloroethane is a suspected carcinogen.
general_note: Vapor irritating. Liquid slightly irritating.

synonyms: Chlorex; Chloroethyl ether; bis(2-Chloroethyl) ether; bis-beta-Chloroethyl ether; DCEE; 2,2'-Dichlorodiethyl ether; Dichloroether; Dichloroethyl ether; beta,beta'-Dichloroethyl ether; sym-Dichloroethyl ether; Dichloroethyl oxide; Ethane, 1,1'-oxybis[2-chloro-; 1,1'-oxybis[2-chloro-; 1,1'-Oxybis[2-chloroethane]
fire_extinguishing_agent: Foam, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Wear full protective clothing and respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: When heated to decomposition, it emits highly toxic fumes; it reacts with water or steam to evolve toxic or corrosive fumes.
symptoms: Nausea, irritation of eyes and nose.
short_term_exposure: 500-1000 ppm causes severe irritation of the eyes and nose after brief exposure. 100 ppm produces slight nausea and irritation.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable until heated to decomposition. Will react with water or steam, and can react vigorously with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Unavailable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, large heavy face shield, self-contained breathing apparatus. Secure ignition sources. Flush with large quantities of water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor is irritant to mucous membranes of eyes and nose. It affects kidneys and liver in varying degrees, and is a mild narcotic.

synonyms: bis(2-Chloroisopropyl)ether; Dichloroisopropyl ether; Ether, bis(2-chloro-1-methylethyl); Propane, 2,2'-oxybis[2-chloro
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water, foam, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Water to blanket fire. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Liberates hydrogen chloride vapors when combustion occurs.
symptoms: Strong respiratory tract irritation and damage to liver and kidneys.
short_term_exposure: The lower lethal concentration for rats in 5 hours was 700 ppm.
first_aid: Remove immediately to fresh air. Administer artificial respiration or oxygen as necessary. For ingestion, provide immediate hospitalization.
stability: Stable. Reacts with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Incompatible with aluminum, copper, epoxy coatings.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear self-containing breathing apparatus, full protective clothing and rubber gloves. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Skin and eye irritation by direct contact.

synonyms: Methylene bichloride; Methylene chloride; Methylene dichloride
appearance: Colorless liquid with a chloroform-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water, foam, dry chemical CO2
special_fire_procedures: Wear self-contained breathing apparatus. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: No flash point by conventional methods, but forms flammable vapor-air mixtures at 212°F and higher. Evolves phosgene, a poisonous gas, and hydrogen chloride gas when heated.
symptoms: Lightheadedness, mental confusion, nausea, vomiting and headache.
short_term_exposure: Not well established, possibly in the range of 10,000 to 20,000 ppm by volume in air. However, incoordination, dizziness and slight nausea begin after a half-hour exposure to approximately 1000 ppm.
first_aid: Give artificial respiration if breathing has stopped. If the eyes are involved, flush and then irrigate with large amounts of water for at least 15 minutes. If ingestion has occurred, obtain medical attention.
stability: Stable; but contact with open flame causes decomposition.
incompatibility: Corrosive to aluminum and magnesium; corrosive to steel when wet.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Vapor causes anesthetic effects at high concentrations. Liquid causes skin and eye irritation. Prolonged or repeated skin contact may cause defatting of the skin and may produce dermatitis from daily contact.
extraction_note: Health Hazard Ratings row printed unclearly in source text ('2) le'); interpreted as '2,1,0' but flagged for visual confirmation.

synonyms: Chlorophenols, liquid; Dichlorophenol; Phenol, 2,4-dichloro-
appearance: White to tan solid needles; colorless liquid; strong medicinal odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water fog, alcohol foam, carbon dioxide, dry chemical.
special_fire_procedures: Water and foam may cause frothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame. May decompose in a fire, releasing toxic products including hydrogen chloride.
symptoms: Irritation, burning, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, hyperactivity, and/or convulsions.
short_term_exposure: Inhalation: Dust and vapor toxic; 15 ppm very irritating.
first_aid: Get medical attention. Inhalation: Remove to fresh air, rest, mouth to mouth resuscitation or oxygen if needed. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting. Give large amounts of milk or water. Skin: Wash with water for 15 to 30 minutes. Eyes: Flush with water for at least 30 minutes.
stability: Stable below 200°C. Reacts with acids and caustic and alkali solutions.
incompatibility: Rapidly corrodes aluminum, slowly corrodes zinc, tin, brass, bronze, copper. Use stainless or mild steel with nitrogen pad (to keep dry). Linings are generally unsuitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact, wear goggles, body covering clothing including rubber or neoprene gloves, gauntlets, and boots. Use self-contained breathing apparatus. For solid spills prevent entry into sewers or natural waterways; shovel into clean dry containers. For liquid spills, dike and let freeze, shovel into dry containers. Do not use water. Material is a serious pollution hazard. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Will irritate skin and burn eyes on short exposure. Possibility of thermal burns from hot liquid.

synonyms: Dichloropropane; Propane, 1,2-dichloro-; Propylene chloride; Propylene dichloride
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Keep exposed tanks cool with water spray. Provide body and respiratory protection for fire parties.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Both the liquid and vapor, on contact with a hot surface or a naked flame, decompose to form phosgene, an extremely poisonous gas. Highly toxic hydrogen chloride gas is a combustion product.
symptoms: Headache, weakness, nausea, dizziness. Skin contact may cause dermatitis.
short_term_exposure: Short-term peak exposures of workmen to 400 to 500 ppm were tolerated without apparent ill effects.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention. Symptoms may be delayed several days or longer.
stability: Generally stable. Can react vigorously with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Corrodes aluminum.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves and protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Skin contact can cause dermatitis. Vapor inhalation causes fatty degeneration of the liver and kidneys.

synonyms: alpha-Chloroallyl chloride; gamma-Chloroallyl chloride; Dichloropropene; 1,3-Dichloropropylene; alpha,gamma-Dichloropropylene; 1-Propene, 1,3-dichloro-; Telone
appearance: White or yellow liquid; sweet penetrating odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Fire parties must wear full respiratory protection and, where danger of skin contact exists, full body protection as well.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Combustion produces toxic vapors of hydrogen chloride, phosgene, and carbon monoxide. Fire may cause violent rupture of tank.
symptoms: Blisters and burns when in contact with skin. Breathing the vapors causes irritation to nose and eyes.
short_term_exposure: Unavailable. However, it should be noted that the commercial product is a mixture of isomers. The physical properties will vary somewhat depending upon the proportion of each isomer present. The mixture should be handled in the same manner as a Class B poison.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Will cause corrosion of steel if wet or at elevated temperatures; also attacks aluminum and rubber.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Liquid is severely irritating to eyes. Vapor is a severe irritant.

synonyms: Cyclopentadiene; 1,3-Cyclopentadiene; 1,3-Cyclopentadiene dimer; Dicy; 3a,4,7,7a-; Dicyclo-1,4-pentadiene; Tetrahydro-4,7-methanoindene
appearance: Colorless crystals or molten liquid; camphor-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Foam, carbon dioxide, dry chemical, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective. Keep exposed tanks cool with water spray.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Keep away from heat, sparks and fire.
symptoms: Inhalation—dizziness, drowsiness. Skin contact—dermatitis following prolonged contact.
short_term_exposure: 1 ppm caused slight eye and throat irritation after 7 minutes. Eye irritation resulted after 10 minutes at 5.5 ppm.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid causes skin and eye irritation. Avoid prolonged or repeated breathing of vapor. Possibility of thermal burns from hot liquid.

synonyms: Diesel fuel; Fuel oil no. 1-D; Fuel oil no. 2-D; Petroleum oil
appearance: Brown, slightly viscous liquid; smells like kerosene
fire_grade: D or E depending on flash point
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Water or foam may cause frothing. Do not direct water directly into fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Diesel fuel, due to its elevated flash point, will generally not constitute a fire hazard. Keep away from heat or flame.
symptoms: Ingestion causes irritation of stomach and intestines with nausea and vomiting. Inhalation: headache, stupor.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, protective clothing. Have respiratory protection available. Secure ignition sources. Soak up with rags, paper, or dry vermiculite. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Inhalation of high concentrations of vapor can cause headache and stupor. Liquid is irritating to the skin.

synonyms: Diethylolamine; 2,2'-Dihydroxydiethylamine; Di-(2-hydroxyethyl)amine; bis(Hydroxyethyl)amine; bis(2-Hydroxyethyl)amine; 2,2'-Iminobisethanol; 2,2'-Iminodiethanol
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, water fog, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Water or foam may cause frothing. Provide fire fighters with self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame. Irritating vapors are generated when heated.
symptoms: Itching or burning at points of contact.
first_aid: Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Relatively stable.
incompatibility: Avoid copper and its alloys.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, face-shield or all-purpose canister respirator, protective clothing. May cover with sodium bisulfate, spray with large excess of water and wash up. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Since the pure material is solid at ambient temperatures, diethanolamine may be carried in aqueous solution or at elevated temperature to keep it liquid. + Unassigned
general_note: Liquid is irritating to skin and highly corrosive to eyes. Avoid inhalation of high vapor concentrations.

synonyms: DEN; N-Ethylethanamine
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical or alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Provide fire fighters with self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Extremely flammable. Dangerous when exposed to heat or flame. Vapors are heavier than air and may travel considerable distance to an ignition source and flashback. Irritating vapors are generated when heated.
symptoms: Liquid causes eye injury and skin irritation.
first_aid: In case of contact with eyes or skin, immediately flush with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes; for eyes get medical attention. Remove contaminated clothing and shoes at once.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Steel and stainless steel are compatible. Copper and its alloys should not be used.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, face-shield or all-purpose canister respirator, protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Cover with sodium bisulfate and clean up. Flush spill with large quantities of water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid very irritating on contact and is toxic by skin absorption. Vapor causes severe irritation of nose and respiratory passages.

synonyms: Diethylbenzene (1,2-, 1,3- or 1,4-); Diethylbenzene, m- or o- isomers
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Fight in the same manner as any Grade D petroleum product fire. Firefighter should wear respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Headache, dizziness, nausea
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention. The effects of inhalation may be delayed.
stability: Relatively stable. Can react with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Rubber, on long immersion, will first swell, then soften.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Usually shipped as a mixture of isomers; the ortho and para forms will predominate.
general_note: Vapor harmful.
extraction_note: Health Hazard Ratings row printed unclearly in source text ('1; 191'); interpreted as '1,1,1' but flagged for visual confirmation.

synonyms: DEG; Diglycol; Dihydroxydiethyl ether; 2,2'-Dihydroxyethyl ether; bis(2-Hydroxyethyl)ether; 3-Oxa-1,5-pentanediol; 2,2'-Oxybisethanol; 2,2'-Oxydiethanol
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Water or foam may cause frothing. Do not direct water directly into fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight hazard, when exposed to heat or flame; can react with oxidizing materials.
symptoms: Skin which has come into contact with the liquid may burn or itch.
first_aid: Eye or skin contact—flush affected area gently with water for 15 minutes. For eye contact, or if skin is blistered or peeled, get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Compatible with most materials of construction.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face-shield, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Under ordinary conditions of handling, not considered toxic.

synonyms: Butoxydiethylene glycol; 2-(2-Butoxy ethoxy) ethanol; Butyl Carbitol; Butyl diglycol; Butyl dioxitol; Diglycol monobutyl ether; Dowanol DB; Ektasolve DB Solvent
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area—CO2, dry chemical. Open area-polar solvent foam
special_fire_procedures: Water spray may cause frothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.

first_aid: Liquid—flush with water. Vapor inhalation—remove victim to fresh air.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Mild steel and stainless steel are suitable. Certain rubbers and plastics are unsuitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Absorb on paper towel and vermiculite. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Slight eye irritation. Low toxicity.

synonyms: Carbitol solvent; Dowanol DE; Ektasolve DE Solvent; Ethoxy diglycol; 2-(2-Ethoxyethoxy)ethanol
fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, alcohol foam or carbon dioxide.
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard when exposed to heat.
symptoms: None expected with normal use.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected area with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice for eye contact.
stability: Stable. Can react with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Absorb on paper towel and vermiculite. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Strong ingestive toxin. Mild local irritant. Under ordinary conditions of handling not considered toxic.

synonyms: Dowanol DM; Ektasolve DM Solvent; 2-(2-Methoxyethoxy)ethanol; Methyl Carbitol
appearance: Colorless liquid with a mild pleasant odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water, carbon dioxide, dry chemical, or alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Liquid may irritate eyes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected area with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice for eye contact.
stability: Stable. Can react with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Not considered toxic under ordinary conditions of handling.

synonyms: bis(2-Aminoethyl)amine; 2,2'-Diaminodiethylamine
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog.
special_fire_procedures: Water increases the amount of vapor produced. Fire parties should wear body and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: At ambient temperatures the fire hazard is low. Irritating vapors are generated when heated.
symptoms: Throat irritation, nausea, wheezing breath. Liquid contact can cause serious eye and skin burns and severe allergic reactions.
short_term_exposure: Unknown. No animal deaths followed on 8-hour exposure to saturated vapors at room temperature.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Oxygen, administered by trained personnel, is helpful. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable. Water dilution will evolve toxic vapors.

unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous, when exposed to heat or flame. Unless the flow of gas can be stopped, extinguishing a fire will permit accumulation of an explosive concentration of vapor, and subsequent explosion or re-flash.
symptoms: Inhalation-headache, dizziness, drowsiness. Skin contact—frostbite.
short_term_exposure: Exposure of guinea pigs to concentrations of from 4.7 to 5.5% for 2 hours caused only slight drowsiness and irregular respiration.
first_aid: Vapor—remove to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Noncorrosive
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister respirator available. Liquid will evaporate rapidly. Secure all possible sources of ignition. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Simple asphyxiant. Breathing vapor may cause unconsciousness without warning because of lack of oxygen. Contact with liquid will cause frostbite.
extraction_note: Boiling point, freezing point, vapor pressure, and vapor density values were not legible in the text layer for this page.

synonyms: Aminoethanol; 2-Aminoethanol; beta-Aminoethyl alcohol; Colamine; Ethylolamine; 2-Hydroxyethylamine; beta-Hydroxyethylamine; Monoethanolamine
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Respiratory and body protection should be worn by fire parties.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame. Irritating vapors generated when heated.
symptoms: Respiratory irritation will range from itching to severe burning depending upon concentration.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Oxygen, administered by trained personnel, is often helpful. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: It will oxidize in the presence of air, so is often shipped under a pad of inert gas. Ethanolamine is a reactive material combining chemically with many other substances.
incompatibility: Corrosive to copper and its alloys; also attacks rubber.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, face shield or all-purpose canister respirator, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Cover spill with sodium bisulfate. Wash with excess of water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid contact causes severe eye irritation. Vapor inhalation causes respiratory irritation.

synonyms: 2-[2-(2-Ethoxyethoxy)ethoxy]ethanol; Ethoxytriethylene glycol; Triethylene glycol ethyl ether; Triglycol ethyl ether; Triglycol monoethyl ether
fire_extinguishing_agent: Carbon dioxide, dry chemical, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Water and foam may be ineffective on fire. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight fire hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: No appreciable hazard in ordinary handling or use.
first_aid: Eye contact—flush gently with water.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Under ordinary conditions of handling, not considered toxic.

synonyms: Acetic acid, ethyl ester; Acetic ester; Acetic ether; Ethyl ethanoate; Vinegar naphtha
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, alcohol foam, water fog, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Use of dry chemical where it can get into a tank of ethyl acetate is not recommended. Fire involving spills outside of tanks can be extinguished with dry chemical.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Ethyl acetate is highly flammable and its vapors form explosive mixtures with air. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Headache, irritation of respiratory passages and eyes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable. Will hydrolize (react with water) on standing to form acetic acid and ethyl alcohol. This reaction is greatly accelerated by bases (alkalies). Can react vigorously with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Softens and dissolves rubber and many plastics.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor causes some irritation. Absorption is chiefly by inhalation. Continued skin contact will dry and crack skin with chance of dermatitis and infection.

synonyms: Acrylic acid, ethyl ester; Ethyl propenoate; Ethyl 2-propenoate; 2-Propenoic acid, ethyl ester
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, water fog, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Keep tank cool with a water spray to prevent polymerization. Wear chemical protective clothing, eye protection and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Ignited by heat, sparks or open flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area. Fire may cause violent rupture of tank. Toxic and irritating vapors generated when heated.
symptoms: Eye and throat irritation, shortness of breath, and convulsions.
short_term_exposure: 50 ppm for 15 minutes. 2000 ppm vapor killed rats in 4 hours with death attributable to severe pulmonary irritation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Will polymerize spontaneously if not inhibited.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
hazardous_polymerization: Will polymerize spontaneously if not inhibited.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Vapor irritating.

synonyms: Alcohol; Alcohol Anhydrous; Alcohol C-2; Cologne spirit; Denatured alcohol; Ethanol; Ethyl hydroxide; Fermentation alcohol; Grain alcohol; Methyl carbinol
appearance: Colorless liquid; smells like wine or shellac thinner
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Water may not be effective unless large quantities are used.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous when exposed to heat or flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Dizziness, double vision, and other classic alcohol intoxication symptoms. These may be accompanied by symptoms such as vomiting, attributable to the denaturant.
short_term_exposure: 5000-10,000 ppm irritates eyes and upper respiratory tract; stupor and drowsiness may result after an hour at this concentration. More than 1000 ppm may cause headache and eye irritation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim for fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Eye contact—gently flush with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
cargo_group: Group 20 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Secure ignition sources. Spills may be flushed away with water, but should not be flushed into a confined space because of the explosion hazard. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: One of the least hazardous industrial organic solvents.

synonyms: Aminoethane; Ethylamine, anhydrous; Monoethylamine
appearance: Colorless liquid or gas; strong ammonia-like odor.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, carbon dioxide, or dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Keep burning tank and tanks adjacent to it cool with a water spray.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Toxic oxides of nitrogen may form in fire. Dangerous. Keep away from heat and open flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Liquid causes eye injury and skin irritation.
first_aid: In case of contact with eyes or skin, immediately flush with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes; for eyes get medical attention. Remove contaminated clothing and shoes at once.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Steel, stainless steel and nickel are compatible. Aluminum and copper should not be used.
cargo_group: Group 7 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: If possible, wear butyl rubber gloves, face shield or all-purpose canister respirator, and protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Cover with sodium bisulfate. Clean up. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Direct contact can cause burns.

synonyms: Ethylamine, aqueous solutions; MEA, 70%; Monoethylamine solution, 70%
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water fog, dry chemical, CO2, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Wear protective clothing, self-contained breathing apparatus, and eye protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Highly flammable vapor. Keep away from ignition sources. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Inhalation: Irritation, coughing, chest pain, pulmonary edema. Ingestion: severe burns of mouth and stomach. Skin and eyes: Severe irritation and burns.
short_term_exposure: High volatility means vapor concentration can easily exceed TLV even at room temperature.
first_aid: Get medical attention. Skin or eye contact: Flush skin and eyes with water for 15 minutes. Inhalation: Remove to fresh air and provide mouth to mouth resuscitation or oxygen as needed.
stability: Stable. Reacts with acids and oxidizers. Reacts explosively with mercury.
incompatibility: Suitable: Stainless steel, mild steel, nickel, tinned iron. Unsuitable: Copper, aluminum, zinc, brass, bronze, galvanized iron, polyethylene, rubber.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact and stay upwind. Eliminate ignition sources. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus or amine-type mask, plastic gloves, face shield, goggles. Wash clothing before reuse. Flush spill area with water. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: This very volatile solution produces a toxic irritating vapor.

synonyms: EB; Ethylbenzol; Phenylethane
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Fight in the same manner as any Grade C petroleum fire. Firefighters should wear self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing and eye protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Irritating vapors are generated when heated. Vapors may travel considerable distances from a source in a flammable concentration. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Irritation to eyes and throat, dizziness and a feeling of chest constriction.
short_term_exposure: 200 ppm for 30 minutes; 1000 ppm irritates skin and mucous membranes. 2000 ppm extremely irritating.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Rubber in prolonged exposure to ethylbenzene first swells, then softens.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapors cause eye irritation, dizziness, narcosis (paralysis), burns of the skin, sensation of chest constriction. Irritation of respiratory tract, conjunctivitis, dermatitis. Exfoliation of large patches of skin and chapped appearance result.

synonyms: 2-Ethylbutanol; 2-Ethyl-1-butanol; 2-Ethyl butyl alcohol; sec-Hexyl alcohol; sec-Pentylcarbinol; Pseudohexyl alcohol
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water spray, dry chemical, foam or CO2.
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water. If a leak or spill has not ignited, use water spray to disperse vapors.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Animals tests show minor skin irritation after 24 hours. Severe surface damage of eye when alcohol in sufficient concentration. No deaths upon ingestion.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Eye and skin contact—gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Secure ignition sources. Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Low toxicity.

synonyms: Chloroethane; Ether, hydrochloric; Hydrochloric ether; Monochloroethane; Muriatic ether
appearance: Colorless gas or liquid; ether-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; CO2, dry chemical, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Fire parties must wear respiratory protection. Keep tanks cool with water spray.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: A highly flammable, volatile liquid; produces highly poisonous phosgene gas when ignited. Unless flow of gas can be stopped, putting out an ethyl chloride fire will permit accumulation of an explosive vapor concentration.
symptoms: Irritating to eyes. Drowsiness and dizziness. Frostbitten areas will be white.
short_term_exposure: Inhalation of 19,000 ppm in air caused partial intoxication in one minute which increased to distinct intoxication with slight analgesia in 12 minutes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and immediately flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Handle frostbitten parts gently. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Dangerous reaction is possible with oxidizing agents. Slow hydrolysis (reaction with water) in presence of salt or fresh water to form toxic and corrosive fumes of hydrogen chloride gas.
incompatibility: Compatible with most materials of construction.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. If water temperature is above 54°F, the ethyl chloride will soon boil off. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. Personnel not wearing respiratory protection should be kept upwind of the spill. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor harmful. Liquid may cause skin or eye injury similar to frostbite.
extraction_note: Health Hazard Ratings second digit printed as '7' in source text, which is out of the normal 0-4 rating scale; preserved as printed rather than corrected, and flagged for visual confirmation.

synonyms: Bicarburetted hydrogen; Elayl; Ethene; Olefiant gas
appearance: Colorless liquid or gas; very faint, sweet odor.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; CO2, dry chemical, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Tanks exposed in fire should be kept cool with a water spray. Attempt to shut off leak. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Unless flow of gas can be stopped, putting out an ethylene fire will permit the accumulation of an explosive vapor concentration. Vapors are anesthetic.
symptoms: Dizziness and drowsiness. Contact with liquid will cause frostbite.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: Ethylene is a reactive compound but must be catalyzed before most reactions take place.
incompatibility: Ethylene is not corrosive.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister available. For a gas leak from a faulty tank, keep concentration of gas below the explosive mixture range by forced ventilation. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. The liquid will rapidly boil away, leaving no residue. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * Ethylene is a gas at temperatures above 48.7°F.
general_note: A simple asphyxiant. High concentrations cause anesthesia.

synonyms: 2-Chlorethanol; 2-Chloroethanol; 2-Chloroethyl alcohol; Ethylene chlorhydrin; Glycol chlorohydrin
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water, CO2, alcohol foam and dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Wear self-contained breathing apparatus and full protective clothing. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame. Dangerous; when heated to decomposition, emits highly toxic fumes of phosgene.
symptoms: Vapor—causes nausea, vomiting, vertigo, incoordination, numbness.
short_term_exposure: Absorption by inhalation or skin may cause death. Inhalation—240 ppm lethal to rats in four hours. Human fatality at 350 ppm for two and one-half hours.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim from vapor and administer oxygen if available. Administer artificial respiration if necessary. If swallowed, induce vomiting. Call a doctor.
stability: Dangerously decomposes at high temperatures.
incompatibility: Steel is satisfactory.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear neoprene gloves, plastic protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus. Provide good ventilation. Secure all ignition sources. Wash skin immediately with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Little margin of safety between early reversible symptoms and fatal intoxication. Fatal amounts may be absorbed by the skin.

synonyms: 2-Cyanoethanol; Glycol cyanohydrin; Hydracrylonitrile; 1-Hydroxy-2-cyanoethane; 3-Hydroxypropanenitrile; 3-Hydroxypropionitrile; beta-Hydroxypropionitrile
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Firefighters should wear self-contained breathing apparatus and full protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: When heated, ethylene cyanohydrin gives off poisonous fumes of cyanides. Reacts with water to produce cyanide gas, which is highly poisonous and flammable vapors.
symptoms: Headache, dizziness, blueness of lips and fingernails.
first_aid: If ingested, induce vomiting at once; vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention. See Medical Kit Information, Appendix B
stability: Avoid basic contamination to prevent polymerization. Stable on prolonged storage. Reacts with water. Reacts vigorously with oxidizing materials, chlorsulfonic acid, oleum, sodium hydroxide, sulfuric acid.
incompatibility: Corrosive to mild steel.
hazardous_polymerization: Avoid basic contamination to prevent polymerization.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid all contact with liquid or vapor. Wear rubber gloves, face shield, full protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Flood with copious amounts of water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Toxic by ingestion. Avoid high vapor concentrations.

synonyms: 1,2-Diaminoethane; 1,2-Ethanediamine; Ethylenediamine, anhydrous
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Because this material can cause severe eye and skin burns and respiratory distress, fire parties must wear full body and respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Ignited by heat and open flame. Irritating vapors are generated when heated.
symptoms: Coughing, redness of eyes, wheezing breath. Liquid contact can cause immediate skin damage and blistering.
short_term_exposure: 400 ppm has been reported to produce immediate and severe irritation to nose and throat.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Oxygen, administered by trained personnel, can prove helpful. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: This is a reactive substance, combining chemically with many others.
incompatibility: Copper and its alloys are corroded readily and should be avoided.
cargo_group: Group 7 compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, all-purpose canister respirator, protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Keep unprotected personnel away from spill. If possible cover with sodium bisulfate. Spray with water. An alternative is to reduce vapor hazard by covering with alcohol foam. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: On-scene supervisors should avoid vapor exposure to persons who have asthma or other respiratory ailments.
general_note: Causes severe burns. Vapor harmful.

synonyms: Bromofume; 1,2-Dibromoethane; sym-Dibromoethane; EDB; Ethane, 1,2-dibromo-; Ethylene bromide; Glycol dibromide
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water spray, dry chemical, foam or CO2
special_fire_procedures: Fire fighters should wear full-protective clothing and respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Ethylene dibromide is difficulty flammable. Dangerous, when heated to decomposition, it emits highly toxic fumes of bromides.
symptoms: Blistering of skin; destruction of tissue.
short_term_exposure: 200 ppm for one hour; 5000 ppm for several minutes might be fatal.
first_aid: Contaminated shoes and clothing should be removed at once and the skin should be thoroughly cleaned with soap and water. If eyes are accidently contaminated they should be flushed thoroughly with flowing water for 15 minutes. A physician should be consulted.
stability: Stable, has no oxidizing or polymerizing characteristics. Will not react with air, water vapor, fresh or salt water at temperatures below 115°F.
incompatibility: Reacts vigorously with aluminum and magnesium. No appreciable attack on steel, wood, or cloth. Softens and deteriorates rubber and paint.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Wash away with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Prolonged contact with skin should be avoided. Toxic by inhalation, skin contact and ingestion.

synonyms: 1,2-Dichloroethane; sym-Dichloroethane; Dutch liquid; Dutch oil; EDC; Ethane, 1,2-dichloro-; Ethylene chloride; Glycol dichloride
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Keep exposed tanks cool with water spray. Water may be ineffective on fire. Supply respiratory protection and full protective clothing for fire parties.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: The vapors are irritating. In contact with a hot surface, ethylene dichloride decomposes into phosgene, which is highly poisonous. Ignited by heat, sparks or open flame.
symptoms: Irritation, dizziness, nausea, rapid pulse, blueness of lips and fingernails.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Relatively stable.
incompatibility: Non-corrosive at normal atmospheric temperatures when dry. When contaminated with water at elevated temperatures it corrodes iron.
cargo_group: Group 36 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Vapor harmful; causes systemic poisoning through inhalation. Liquid contact on skin may cause dermatitis or a burn. Toxic by inhalation, skin contact and ingestion.
extraction_note: NOTE: Detectable odor is greater than the TLV. Exposure to potentially dangerous vapor concentrations can occur before the vapor is detected by smell.

unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight hazard when exposed to heat or flame.

short_term_exposure: Inhalation is no hazard at normal room temperatures.
first_aid: Ingestion: induce vomiting and call a physician. Never give fluids or induce vomiting if victim is unconscious or having convulsions. Skin and eyes: flush with water for 10 minutes.

incompatibility: Most materials of construction are suitable.

general_note: Relatively non-toxic unless ingested. If ingested, serious injury or death may result from as little as 60 ml (approx. 2 oz.).

appearance: Colorless oily liquid; mild rancid odor

unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.

first_aid: Prevent repeated skin contact by wearing protective clothing.

incompatibility: Compatible with usual materials of construction. Plastic materials and rubber are not recommended.

general_note: Eye and respiratory tract irritation, narcosis, blood, kidney, and to a lesser degree, liver damage can be produced in animals from a single or repeated exposures at concentrations less than saturation.

spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Low toxicity
