fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: The same techniques used for fighting fires involving combustible petroleum products are applicable. Cool fire exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Drowsiness, confusion, loss of mental ability, headache.
first_aid: Vapor—remove the victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: This is a relatively stable compound.
incompatibility: Softens many plastics.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Harmful vapor; liquid absorption through the skin may be harmful.

synonyms: Anprolene; Dimethylene oxide; EO; Epoxyethane; 1,2-Epoxyethane; Oxirane
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; CO2, dry chemical, water fog
special_fire_procedures: It is important to keep the temperature of storage tank low; use large amounts of water. Approach only after considering explosion danger. Keep firefighting personnel behind cover if practicable. If the water supply is inadequate or the tank shows signs of overheating, evacuate the area.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Irritating vapors generated when heated. Flammable—does not need oxygen for combustion. If local "hot spots" develop in the tank, the liquid in the tank may explode.
symptoms: Burning sensation in eyes, nose and throat; dizziness and headache.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical attention immediately.
stability: Ethylene oxide's tendency to polymerize increases rapidly when the temperature goes above 30°C. It will decompose with explosive violence when the temperature reaches 571°C.
incompatibility: May polymerize violently when in contact with highly active catalytic surfaces such as anhydrous iron, tin and aluminum chlorides, pure iron and aluminum oxides and alkali metal hydroxides. Do not use copper, silver or their alloys.
hazardous_polymerization: Tendency to polymerize increases rapidly above 30°C; may polymerize violently in contact with certain catalytic surfaces.
cargo_group: Unassigned in the compatibility chart. For compatibility assistance, call G-MTH-1 (202-267-1577).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, large heavy face shield (if in doubt use body shield also) and self-contained breathing apparatus. Secure ignition sources. Avoid contact with liquid. Flush with large quantities of water. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. Notify local fire department. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Moderate hazard, for both acute and chronic exposures. Volatility is high and pulmonary absorption is rapid.

synonyms: Anesthesia ether; Anesthetic ether; Diethyl ether; Diethyl oxide; Ethane, 1,1'-oxybis-; Ether; Ethoxyethane; Ethyl oxide; 1,1'-Oxybisethane; Solvent ether; Sulfuric ether
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Cool tank with water spray. Keep surroundings cool to reduce the amount of vapors produced. The danger of reignition is high.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: A highly flammable, volatile liquid with a wide explosive range and low autoignition temperature. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Exhilaration may be experienced first followed by drowsiness and unconsciousness. Contact with the skin may cause dermatitis.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Oxygen, when administered by trained personnel, is helpful. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: In the presence of air, ether forms ethyl peroxide, which may explode if heated.
incompatibility: Compatible with most of the usual materials of construction. Ether swells natural rubber, so protective clothing should be made of plastic which resists ether.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, large heavy face shield (if in doubt use body shield also). Have self-contained breathing apparatus available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure all ignition sources. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. If a spill occurs into navigable water, the ether will float downstream and create a severe fire hazard until it has all vaporized. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Ethyl ether is a volatile liquid possessing irritative and narcotic properties. Absorption of excessive quantities by any route may lead progressively to a state of intoxication, loss of consciousness and death due to respiratory failure.

synonyms: Alcohol C-8; 2-Ethyl-1-hexanol; 2-Ethylhexyl alcohol; Octanol; Octyl alcohol
appearance: Colorless, slightly viscous liquid; alcoholic odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, CO2, dry chemical, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Mild skin irritation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing. Flush affected areas gently with water for 15 minutes; 20-30 minutes for eye contact. Get medical attention.
stability: Will undergo self-reaction if contaminated. Does not require stabilizer.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Practically non-hazardous. Slight effect from absorption of liquid through skin.

synonyms: Acrylic acid, 2-ethylhexyl ester; 2-Ethylhexyl, 2-propenoate; Octyl acrylate
fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, CO2, foam, water
special_fire_procedures: Water or foam may cause frothing. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame; will polymerize on heating.
symptoms: Skin irritation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush with water.
stability: Unstable; polymerizes easily unless inhibited.
incompatibility: Non-corrosive to carbon steel.
hazardous_polymerization: Polymerizes easily unless inhibited.
spill_or_leak_procedure: If possible, wear rubber gloves, face shield, and protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. Flush spill away with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid irritating to skin on contact.

synonyms: Alkyl (C7-C9) nitrates; Mixed octyl nitrates; Octyl nitrates
appearance: Light yellow liquid; ester, fruity odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water fog, foam, dry chemical, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Avoid breathing vapor. Can explode if heated while confined—cool storage container with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Combustible—gives off toxic nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide gases when heated or burned.
symptoms: Mild skin and eye irritation on contact. Inhalation produces headaches, dizziness, nausea, and low blood pressure.
short_term_exposure: Low health risk from inhalation unless the liquid is heated to decomposition or mist is formed.
first_aid: Ingestion: If conscious, drink water, induce vomiting. Inhalation: Remove to fresh air. Skin: Flush with soap and water. Eyes: Flush with water for at least 15 minutes.
stability: Stable at ambient temperature, decomposes when heated. Can explode if heated to high temperatures while confined. Reacts with strong oxides, strong bases, strong reducing agents.
incompatibility: Suitable: Mild steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, zinc, tin, brass, bronze, neoprene, nitrile rubber. Unsuitable: Butyl rubber, ethylene-propylene rubber.
cargo_group: Group 34 of the compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact, especially vapor. Secure all ignition sources. Wear goggles and neoprene or nitrile gloves—use self-contained breathing apparatus if needed. Dike spill, soak up with sand or earth; dispose by controlled burning. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: When heated, decomposes to form nitrogen oxides. Low toxicity by ingestion and inhalation; slightly toxic by skin contact.

synonyms: 5-Ethylidene bicyclo(2,2,1)hept-2-ene; Ethylidene norbornylene; Ethylidene norcamphene
appearance: Colorless liquid with a turpentine-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Carbon dioxide, dry chemical, foam
special_fire_procedures: Wear protective clothing. Water may be ineffective on fire. Cool exposed containers with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous fire hazard.
symptoms: Inhalation—vapors cause headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and respiratory distress. Ingestion—irritation of entire digestive system. Irritates eyes and skin.
short_term_exposure: Prolonged exposure to vapor proved toxic to rats.
first_aid: Remove contaminated clothing and flush affected areas with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes. Remove victim to fresh air. Administer artificial respiration if necessary. If ingested, induce vomiting. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable at temperatures below 200°C, but unstable above 350°C, decomposing rapidly in presence of air.
incompatibility: Non-corrosive to steel, stainless steel and aluminum. Glass, "Teflon" and ceramics are acceptable.
cargo_group: Group 30 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, face shield and protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderate skin irritant. Excessive contact with skin should be avoided.
extraction_note: Vapor density value (44) is inconsistent with the molecular weight of this compound as printed; preserved as printed in the source rather than corrected.

synonyms: Ethyl 2-methacrylate; Ethyl alpha-methacrylate; Ethyl 2-methyl-2-propenoate; Methacrylic acid, ethyl ester; 2-Propenoic acid, 2-methyl-, ethyl ester
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, chemical foam
special_fire_procedures: Easily forms explosive mixtures with air. Remove all sources of flames, sparks or other ignition sources. Electrical devices should be grounded and bonded. Cool tanks with water fog.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Fire may cause violent rupture of tank due to polymerization. Forms explosive mixtures with air in the presence of heat or flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if heated in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Skin allergy develops, vapor causes corneal ulceration, visual disturbance, irritation to respiratory tract, lack of appetite, nausea, convulsion, coma.
short_term_exposure: 100 ppm over 8 hours. Animal tests show effects are not cumulative.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Immediately flush affected area with water, use mild soap and water for skin exposure. Experiments have shown Ethyl Methacrylate to be a teratogen; this means that physical defects can be produced in the developing embryo.
stability: Polymerizes; inhibitor required. Can react with oxidizing agents. Ground storage drums or tanks to prevent accumulation of static electricity.
incompatibility: Glass, types 316 and 304 stainless steel, or aluminum are suitable; corrosive to mild steel.
hazardous_polymerization: Polymerizes; inhibitor required.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Protective clothing, goggles, neoprene gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus should be worn. Flush spills with water fog. Dike flaming pools and extinguish using chemical foams. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderately toxic, liquid causes skin irritation. Vapors mildly irritating.

synonyms: 2-Ethyl hexanal; 2-Ethyl-2-hexanal; 2-Ethyl-3-propyl acyraldehyde
appearance: Yellow liquid; sharp, powerful, irritating odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, water fog, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: The vapors of this chemical are highly irritating. For this reason, respiratory protection is necessary. In other respects, firefighting techniques will be the same as for a Grade E Petroleum product.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Burning sensation in respiratory passages or on skin in contact with the liquid.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Unavailable
cargo_group: Group 19 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Small spills may be washed away with water. For large spill, cover with sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3). Add small amounts of water and mix. Scoop up. Wash site with soap solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor is irritating to respiratory passages. Liquid irritating to skin.

synonyms: Formalin; Formalith; Formic aldehyde solution; Formol; Fyde; Methanal solution; Methylene oxide; Morbicid
fire_grade: D or E: Combustible liquid (grade depends on concentration)
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: The vapors are highly irritating, so fire parties should wear respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: When the solution is heated, highly flammable vapors are given off.
symptoms: Coughing, copious watering of eyes, severe respiratory irritation.
short_term_exposure: At a vapor concentration of 10 to 20 ppm breathing becomes difficult. Exposure to 650 ppm for a few minutes may cause death.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Solutions are often shipped at elevated temperatures to prevent polymer formation.
incompatibility: Corrosive to steel and to copper and its alloys.
hazardous_polymerization: Solutions are often shipped at elevated temperatures to prevent polymer formation.
cargo_group: Group 19 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition source. If possible, cover large spills with sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3). Add small amount of water and mix. Scoop up. Wash site with soap solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: The commercial material is shipped as water solution of from about 37% to 50% concentration. Methanol is often used to inhibit polymerization. * Proposed change in TLV to 0.3 ppm. † Unavailable
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Major effect is focal irritation of eyes, nose, and throat. Strong formaldehyde solutions cause a hardening effect and primary skin irritation upon direct contact.

synonyms: Formylic acid; Hydrogencarboxylic acid; Methanoic acid
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Firefighting parties should wear rubber boots and gauntlets and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Formic acid is a corrosive, combustible liquid. Toxic vapors are generated in fires.
symptoms: Choking, respiratory irritation, watering of the eyes; skin contact will cause severe itching or burning.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and immediately flush affected areas gently with water for 15 minutes. Get medical attention. Use protective clothing to prevent personal contact.
stability: Reacts with bases (alkalis) to produce heat. It is also a reducing agent.
incompatibility: Type 316, stainless steel or lead-lined tanks are satisfactory.
cargo_group: Group 4 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Use respiratory protection and protective clothing. Eliminate all sources of ignition. Cover contaminated surfaces and spill with large quantities of soda ash or sodium bicarbonate. Mix and add water if necessary for good mixing. Scoop up slurry. Wash site with soda ash solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Natural, slow decomposition yields carbon monoxide (CO), a chemical asphyxiant, and water. Enclosed spaces must be tested for oxygen content (19.5% min.) before entering. Vapor irritating. Liquid causes burns.

synonyms: Genetron; Isotron; Halon; Refrigerant gas; Ucon
appearance: Colorless liquid or gas; sweetish odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Non-flammable
special_fire_procedures: In contact with hot surfaces or a naked flame these compounds form phosgene, an extremely poisonous gas. Keep tanks, adjacent to fire, cool with water spray. Fire fighters wear full protective clothing including self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Freon 11, 12, and 114 do not burn. Freon 22 and 113 when heated can form weakly combustible mixtures.
symptoms: Drowsiness with or without nausea.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. If breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Get medical attention. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten, handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: Chemically stable, but see Special Fire Procedures above.
incompatibility: Compatible with most materials of construction.
hazardous_decomposition_products: Phosgene (contact with hot surfaces or flame).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. The liquid may boil away (see below) at ambient temperature. Extinguish open flames in vicinity of the spill in order to avoid generation of phosgene. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Formula/Freon/Halon/Boiling Point/CHRIS Code table: CCl3F=Freon 11=Halon 113=+74.8°F=TCF; CCl2F2=Freon 12=Halon 122=-21.6°F=DCF; CHClF2=Freon 22=Halon 121=-41.4°F=MCF; CCl2FCClF2=Freon 113=Halon 233=+117.6°F=TTF; CClF2CClF2=Freon 114=Halon 242=+38.4°F=DTE.
general_note: Vapors are non-irritating to eyes, nose, throat, lungs, and skin, very low toxicity.
extraction_note: The Freon isomer table in Remarks was reconstructed from a garbled OCR table; boiling points for Freon 12 and 22 were re-derived from known CHRIS codes (DCF, MCF) since the printed figures were corrupted — flagged for visual confirmation.

synonyms: Ant oil, artificial; Artificial oil of ants; Fural; 2-Furaldehyde; 2-Furancarbonal; 2-Furancarboxaldehyde; Furfuraldehyde; Furfuran carboxylic aldehyde; Furfurole; Furole; Pyromucic aldehyde
appearance: Colorless to reddish-brown liquid; penetrating almond-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Wear eye protection, self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame. Furfural can explode on contact with strong mineral acids and alkalis (caustics). Irritating vapors are generated when heated.
symptoms: Irritation of respiratory passages.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Furfural can explode on contact with strong mineral acids and alkalis. Reacts with numerous organic materials.
incompatibility: Dissolves or softens many plastics and rubber formulations.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves and protective clothing. Have self-contained breathing apparatus available. Avoid contact with liquid. Small spills may be washed away with water. Cover large spills with sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3). Add small amount of water and mix. Scoop up. Wash site with soap solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid is irritating to skin and eyes on contact. Vapor is respiratory irritant.

synonyms: 2-Furancarbinol; 2-Furanmethanol; Furfuralcohol; Furylcarbinol; 2-Furylcarbinol; alpha-Furylcarbinol; 2-Furylmethanol; 2-Hydroxymethylfuran
appearance: Colorless-amber liquid turning to dark red-brown when exposed to light and air. Slight brine-like odor.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area—CO2, dry chemical. Open area—polar solvent foam, water spray.
special_fire_procedures: Wear eye protection, clothing resistant to furfuryl alcohol, respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight explosion hazard when exposed to heat or flame. However it will react with explosive violence in contact with mineral acids or their vapors, or with strong organic acids or their vapors.
symptoms: Headaches, watering eyes, irritated skin.
short_term_exposure: Vapor exposures—Rats show 8 percent mortality after one six hour exposure to 47 ppm and 100 percent mortality at 243 and above. Absorption through skin is very rapid.
first_aid: Eyes—wash with water for 10 minutes. Remove contaminated clothing and wash. Skin—wash with soap and water. Ingestion—induce vomiting. Inhalation—move to fresh air. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable. Reactive with organic or mineral acids.
incompatibility: Do not use near lacquers, varnish, or resins. Can ship in ordinary steel.
cargo_group: Group 20 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Spill area may be washed with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Ground storage drums or tanks to prevent accumulation of static electricity.
general_note: Skin absorption may cause toxic effects. Harmful if swallowed. Toxic concentrations of vapors may be present at temperatures above room temperature.

synonyms: Benzin; Motor spirit; Petrol
appearance: Colorless to straw-white liquid; sweet, pleasant odor—gasoline
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam water fog
special_fire_procedures: Tanks exposed to fire should be kept cool with a water spray. Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous fire and explosion hazard in presence of heat or flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Inhalation: Marked vertigo, inability to walk a straight line, hilarity, incoordination, intense burning in throat and lungs, possibly bronchopneumonia, nausea, vomiting.
short_term_exposure: 0.5 to 1.6% vapor concentration was fatal to a man after 5 minutes exposure; 500 to 30,000 ppm was fatal to a youth.
first_aid: Inhalation: Immediately remove victim from contaminated atmosphere. If breathing is interrupted, artificial respiration should be applied immediately. A physician should be called.
stability: Chemically stable.
incompatibility: Almost any usual material of construction is suitable. Natural rubber is softened and will deteriorate rapidly.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear polyethylene gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. Small spills may be flushed away with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid irritating to skin and eyes on contact. Vapor inhalation leads to intoxication.

synonyms: Cidex; 1,3-Diformylpropane; Glutaral; Glutaric dialdehyde; Glutarol; Pentanedial; 1,5-Pentanedial
appearance: Light yellow liquid; rotten apple odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Non-flammable
special_fire_procedures: None
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Will decompose if heated (greater than approximately 400°C) to yield carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, hydrocarbons.
symptoms: Extended exposures result in irritation of respiratory tract. Ingestion yields irritation of mouth and stomach.
short_term_exposure: The lowest lethal concentration for rats in 4 hours is 5000 ppm.
first_aid: Immediately flush with plenty of water for 15 minutes. For ingestion, give large amounts of water and induce vomiting if conscious.
stability: Stable, but decomposes thermally about 400°C forming carbon oxides and hydrocarbons.
incompatibility: Mildly corrosive to mild steel, aluminum, copper, zinc, tin, brass and bronze.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Flush with water. Wear goggles or face shield and rubber gloves. Prevent water contamination. Toxic to fish. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderate irritation to the skin.

synonyms: Glycerol; Glycyl alcohol; 1,2,3-Propanetriol; Trihydroxypropane; 1,2,3-Trihydroxypropane
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Slight hazard, when exposed to heat, flame, or powerful oxidizers.
symptoms: Contact with the liquid can cause skin irritation.
first_aid: Wash glycerine from skin with water. Launder clothing contaminated by the liquid.
stability: Reacts with strong oxidizing agents. Polymerizes about 300°F.
incompatibility: No apparent effect on steel or aluminum.
hazardous_polymerization: Polymerizes about 300°F.
cargo_group: Group 20 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Secure ignition sources. Spills may be washed away with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Even a small amount of water or other impurity will greatly lower the freezing point. + Unassigned
general_note: Skin contact with liquid causes slight skin irritation.
extraction_note: The molecular formula and boiling/freezing point fields printed on this source page do not match glycerine chemically (the formula field shows what appears to be diacetone alcohol's formula, an apparent page/print error in the source); left null rather than supplying the correct chemical formula from outside knowledge, per extraction rules.

synonyms: Dipropylmethane; n-Heptane; Heptyl hydride; Normal heptane
appearance: Volatile, colorless liquid; sweet gasoline-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area—CO2, dry chemical. Open area—foam.
special_fire_procedures: Fire fighters should have respiratory devices. Keep fire exposed containers cool with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Highly flammable, dangerous fire risk. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Irritation of mucous membranes, dizziness, slight nausea, intoxication.
short_term_exposure: 1000 ppm for 6 minutes developed slight dizziness. 500 ppm for 15 minutes results in a condition resembling intoxication by ethyl alcohol.
first_aid: If inhaled in conc. amounts, remove victim to fresh air and use oxygen. If splashed in eyes, wash with water for 15 minutes. Call a doctor.
stability: Non-reactive but dangerous fire risk. Keep away from heat, sparks, or open flame.
incompatibility: Mild steel and stainless steel are suitable. Natural rubber will soften and deteriorate rapidly.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Have all-purpose canister masks available. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderately toxic by inhalation.

synonyms: Azacycloheptane; Hexahydroazepine; Homopiperidine
appearance: Colorless to light yellow liquid; ammonia-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Wear eye protection and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Toxic oxides of nitrogen may form in fire. Dangerous fire hazard. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Eye, skin and respiratory irritation.
short_term_exposure: The approximate lethal vapor concentration for a four hour exposure is reported to be 4800 ppm in rats.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Oxygen, administered by trained personnel, is often helpful. Skin or eye contact—immediately flood affected areas gently with water. Remove contaminated clothing and continue to flush affected areas for 15 minutes. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Corrodes copper and its alloys in air; corrodes aluminum especially when wet. Removes paint; swells rubber. No effect on carbon steel, wood, cloth.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Self-contained breathing apparatus or all-purpose canister mask should be worn when contact is anticipated. Wear impervious gloves and safety goggles. Keep away from heat, sparks and open flames; avoid breathing of vapors. Flush spill with large quantities of water. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid is irritating to the skin and respiratory tract and the vapor causes eye injury. High vapor concentration may cause serious eye injury.

synonyms: 2-Methyl pentane
fire_grade: B or C: Flammable liquid depending on flash point and Reid Vapor Pressure.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Carbon dioxide, dry chemical, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Cool containers with water if exposed to fire. Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous. Keep away from sparks, heat, or open flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Inhalation causes irritation of respiratory tract, cough, mild depression, cardiac arrhythmia. Aspiration causes severe irritation of lungs, coughing, pulmonary edema; excitement followed by depression. Ingestion causes nausea, vomiting, swelling of abdomen, headache, depression.
first_aid: Inhalation: maintain respiration, give oxygen, if needed. Aspiration: enforce bed rest; administer oxygen. Ingestion: DO NOT induce vomiting. Get medical attention or advice. Eyes: wash with copious amounts of water. Skin: wipe off, wash with soap and water.
stability: Dangerous; keep away from sparks, heat, or open flame. Can react vigorously with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
cargo_group: Group 31 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor slightly irritating. Liquid causes slight skin irritation on contact.

synonyms: Hexane; Hexyl hydride; Normal hexane
fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, foam or carbon dioxide.
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire. Cool fire exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Inhalation causes irritation of respiratory tract cough and mild depression. Aspiration causes severe lung irritation, coughing and pulmonary edema. Ingestion causes nausea, vomiting, swelling of abdomen, headache and depression.
short_term_exposure: 30,000 ppm vapor concentration causes narcosis of rats in one hour. 0.5% vapor concentration caused distinct dizziness and giddiness of humans in just ten minutes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove from area and administer artificial respiration, if necessary, and then oxygen. Eye-wash immediately with copious amounts of water. Ingestion—DO NOT induce vomiting. Get medical attention or advice.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Certain plastics are unsuitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield and protective clothing. Have all purpose canister mask available. Gas leak—keep concentration of gas below explosive limits by forced ventilation. Liquid—absorb on paper and discharge paper. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Minor skin irritant. Irritation caused by vapor inhalation. n-Hexane is toxic by ingestion.

synonyms: Alcohol C-6; Amyl carbinol; 1-Hexanol; n-Hexanol; Hexanols; Hexyl alcohol; n-Hexyl alcohol; 1-Hydroxyhexane; Pentylcarbinol
fire_extinguishing_agent: Carbon dioxide, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Similar to alcohol intoxication.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable. May soften some paints and plastics.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear chemical gloves and goggles. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Practically non-toxic. Handle as a detergent.

synonyms: 2-Methyl-2,4-pentanediol; Trimethyltrimethylene glycol; alpha,alpha,alpha'-Trimethyltrimethylene glycol
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Water or foam may cause frothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Headache, dizziness, nausea; strong local irritation of the eyes, nose, and throat; and respiratory discomfort.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Give artificial respiration if necessary. Wash spilled liquid from skin with water. Get medical attention if rash develops or if victim has any breathing difficulty.
stability: Reacts with strong oxidizing agents.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor irritating to skin and eyes at high concentrations. Liquid very irritating to eyes, slightly irritating to skin.

synonyms: Chlorohydric acid; Hydrogen chloride; Muriatic acid
appearance: Colorless to light yellow liquid; irritating, pungent odor
fire_grade: Non-flammable. Classified as a corrosive liquid.
electrical_group: B (based upon possible hydrogen gas (H2) generation should a leak or spill occur)
fire_extinguishing_agent: Non-flammable
special_fire_procedures: Acid tanks exposed to a fire should be cooled by a water spray. Fire parties must wear respiratory protection in order to avoid breathing acid vapor. Full protective clothing must also be worn.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Hydrochloric acid will not burn. It will react with many metals, giving off hydrogen gas which is highly flammable. If hydrogen is trapped in confined spaces, it can form an explosive mixture with air. See data sheet for hydrogen. Toxic and irritating vapors are generated when heated.
symptoms: Where touched by liquid, the skin may tingle or burn. Breathing the vapors will cause severe coughing and watering of the eyes.
short_term_exposure: Inhalation of 1500 ppm in air are fatal in a few minutes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Oxygen, administered by trained personnel, is often helpful. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Reacts with bases (caustics) to generate heat.
incompatibility: Corrodes many metals, causing the evolution of hydrogen gas. Iron and aluminum are corroded readily.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Have body shield available. Secure ignition sources. If possible, cover the contaminated surface and spill with sodium bicarbonate or a soda ash, slaked lime mixture (50-50). Mix and add water if necessary to form a slurry. Scoop up slurry. Wash site with soda ash solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * PEL and TLV based upon hydrogen chloride gas.
general_note: Inhalation of gas results primarily in irritation of upper respiratory passages. Liquid severely irritating to skin and eyes.

synonyms: LH2; Liquid hydrogen; Protium
fire_extinguishing_agent: First stop flow of gas. CO2, dry chemical, water
special_fire_procedures: Source of hydrogen MUST be eliminated before fire is put out to prevent accumulation of explosive vapors. If the insulation fails on a liquid hydrogen tank exposed to fire, the tank will explode; evacuate firefighters and have them take cover.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Will react violently with strong oxidizers. Will ignite easily with oxygen. Vapors form explosive or combustible mixture with air over a wide range of concentrations. Flame is almost invisible. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Inhalation: Drowsiness and high-pitched, squeaky voice. Skin contact: Numbness and whitening of skin at the area of contact.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention immediately. Avoid sparks and open flames.
stability: Will ignite readily when exposed to spark source. Liquid hydrogen will flash into vapor at temperature above -400°F resulting in a sudden and large increase in pressure if confined.
incompatibility: Mild steel and most iron alloys become brittle at liquid hydrogen temperatures. Aluminum and stainless steel (300 series) may be used.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Secure all nearby ignition sources immediately. Isolate spill area and call local fire department and the Captain of the Port, U.S. Coast Guard. If the liquid does not catch fire, it will soon boil off and leave no residue. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Simple asphyxiant. Not considered toxic. Avoid skin contact with liquid.
extraction_note: Boiling point and freezing point values were not legible in the text layer for this page. Note: This cargo is currently not permitted to be shipped in bulk in U.S. waters (per source page note).

synonyms: Albone; High-strength hydrogen peroxide; Hioxyl; Hydrogen dioxide; Hydroperoxide; Peroxide; Superoxol
appearance: Colorless watery liquid; slightly sharp odor.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Non-flammable
special_fire_procedures: Powerful oxidizer. Wear protective clothing including self-contained breathing apparatus. Flood discharge area with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Not flammable but may cause fire and react violently with combustibles and metals. Powerful oxidizer. May cause fire and explode on contact with combustibles and metals.
symptoms: Vapors cause eye and nose discomfort in moderate concentrations; less than 52% causes temporary irritation. Above 52% can cause blisters and eye damage.
first_aid: Avoid contact, immediately flush with water. If ingested give water, induce vomiting if conscious. Remove contaminated clothing and shoes.
stability: Pure grades are stable, but contamination with metals or dirt can cause violent or rapid decomposition.
incompatibility: Incompatible with iron, copper, brass, bronze, chromium, zinc, lead, manganese, silver, and catalytic metals.
cargo_group: Unassigned in compatibility chart. For compatibility assistance, call G-MTH-1 (202-267-1577).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear protective inner and outer clothing, impermeable apron, neoprene gloves. Flush area with water. Isolate material from contacting flammable liquids or combustible materials. Evacuate area for at least 1/2 mile if fire exists. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor is irritating.

synonyms: Ethylene glycol monoacrylate; HEA; beta-Hydroxyethyl acrylate; 2-Hydroxyethyl 2-propenoate
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, water, alcohol foam.
special_fire_procedures: Wear eye protection, self-contained breathing apparatus, and impermeable protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard; however, dangerous when exposed to high temperatures due to liberation of toxic fumes.
symptoms: Watering of eyes, red or irritated skin.
short_term_exposure: Avoid inhalation of hot vapors. Irritation of skin upon short contact; burn after prolonged contact. Animal tests show no deaths after ingestion.
first_aid: If swallowed, induce vomiting; remove victim to fresh air if any ill effects from breathing vapors are felt. Flush eyes and skin immediately after contact for approximately 15 minutes. Call a doctor.
stability: No spontaneous decomposition, but can polymerize.
incompatibility: Corrodes mild steel, tin plate, and polymerizes. No effect on stainless steel, aluminum, or mild steel with phenolic resin surfaces. Swells rubber, removes paints.
hazardous_polymerization: Can polymerize; corrodes mild steel and tin plate in the process.
cargo_group: Unassigned in compatibility guide. See Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear eye protection. Neoprene rubber or other impermeable protective clothing should be worn. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Severe eye damage, irritated skin, serious illness after ingestion. Class B poison.
