synonyms: Isoacetophenone; 3,5,5-Trimethyl-2-cyclohexene-1-one
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water spray, carbon dioxide, dry chemical or foam.
special_fire_procedures: Use water spray to disperse vapors. Water may be used to flush spills.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Eye, nose, and throat irritation; narcosis.
short_term_exposure: 25 ppm is an irritant to most humans. Animal tests resulted in eye injury and slight skin irritation after 24 hours; inhalation killed 1 of 6 animals in 8 hours.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air and use oxygen. Flush eyes for 15 minutes with water. Wash off skin. Get medical help.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Steel is satisfactory.
cargo_group: Group 18 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, and protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Keep unprotected personnel upwind. Flush spill with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Highly toxic, strong irritant to skin and eyes.

synonyms: beta-Methylbivinyl; 2-Methyl-1,3-butadiene; 3-Methyl-1,3-butadiene
fire_extinguishing_agent: Carbon dioxide, dry chemical, foam
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water spray.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: In a fire, polymerization may occur and violently rupture the container. It is recommended that isoprene be stored under an inert atmosphere (preferably nitrogen) with at least 50 ppm tert-butylcatechol present as an inhibitor. Keep away from sparks, heat or open flame.
symptoms: Vapor—Eye and upper respiratory tract irritant. Liquid may irritate eyes.
short_term_exposure: No data on human exposure are available but concentrations of 5% in air are fatal to mice.
first_aid: Remove to fresh air. In case of contact with liquid immediately flush skin or eyes with water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated clothing and shoes at once. Call a physician.
stability: Readily oxidized, polymerized. Should be inhibited to prevent polymerization.
incompatibility: May soften some types of rubber or paint.
hazardous_polymerization: Readily polymerized; should be inhibited to prevent polymerization.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Isoprene is an irritant to mucous membranes of the eyes, nose, and upper respiratory passages.

synonyms: Coal oil; Fuel oil no. 1; Illuminating oil; Kerosine; Range oil
appearance: Pale yellow to water white oily liquid; strong odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area—CO2, dry chemical. Open area—foam, water fog.
special_fire_procedures: Tanks exposed to fire should be kept cool with a water spray. Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flammable, moderate risk.
symptoms: Inhalation: Marked vertigo, inability to walk a straight line, hilarity, incoordination, intense burning in throat and lungs, possibly bronchopneumonia, nausea, vomiting.
first_aid: Inhalation: Remove victim from contaminated atmosphere. If breathing is interrupted, artificial respiration should be applied immediately. Call a doctor.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Most metals are suitable, but kerosene causes rusting of steel.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. Small spills may be flushed away with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderately toxic by ingestion and inhalation.

synonyms: LNG; Methane, refrigerated liquid; Natural gas, refrigerated liquid
appearance: Colorless liquefied gas; usually odorized to give a weak skunk like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; Dry chemical for small fires.
special_fire_procedures: Use water to cool exposed tanks. Do not extinguish large spill fires. Allow to burn while cooling adjacent equipment with water spray.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Containers may explode in fire. Vapor may travel to ignition source and flash back along vapor trail. Unless the flow of gas can be stopped, putting out an LNG fire will permit the accumulation of an explosive concentration of vapor and subsequent explosion or reflash.
symptoms: If concentration of gas is high enough, may cause asphyxiation. No systemic effect even at 5% concentration in air.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to open air. Administer artificial respiration if necessary. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Stainless steel, nickel steel and aluminum are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. Call fire department. For leak from faulty tank keep concentration below flammable limits by forced ventilation. If the LNG does not catch fire, it will soon boil off. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapors are non-irritating to eyes and throat. Liquid will cause frostbite.

synonyms: Bottled gas; LPG; Petroleum gases, liquefied; Propane-Butane mixtures; Pyrofax
appearance: Colorless compressed gas, with faint skunk odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; Water (Let fire burn)
special_fire_procedures: Allow to burn while cooling adjacent equipment with water. Shut off leak if possible.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Containers may explode in fire. Vapor is heavier than air and may travel a long distance to a source of ignition and flash back. Unless the flow of gas can be stopped, putting out an LPG fire will permit the accumulation of an explosive concentration of vapor and subsequent explosion or reflash.
symptoms: Concentration in air greater than 10% causes dizziness in a few minutes. High concentration cause asphyxiation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to open air. Administer artificial respiration if necessary. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Stainless steel, nickel steel and aluminum are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. Call fire department. For leak from faulty tanks, keep concentration below flammable limits by forced ventilation. If the LPG does not catch fire, it will soon boil off. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Not irritating to eyes, nose or throat. If inhaled, will cause dizziness. Liquid will cause frostbite.

synonyms: cis-Butenedioic anhydride; 2,5-Furandione
appearance: Colorless liquid, white solid (as needles, crystals or fused tablets); acrid, choking odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, carbon dioxide
special_fire_procedures: Water and foam can cause frothing. Can react with dry chemical. Keep tanks cool in fire by spraying water on them from safe distance. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus, and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Mild fire hazard. Inertion with nitrogen recommended to avoid reaction with water vapor. When heated, can decompose and overpressurize storage tanks.
symptoms: Inhalation: Moderately irritating, coughing, sneezing, bronchitis from chronic exposure. Skin: Irritation, redness; dermatitis from chronic exposure. Eyes: Irritation, can be severe, tearing. Ingestion: Little or no risk; nausea.
short_term_exposure: Limited inhalation risk if space well ventilated.
first_aid: Ingestion: Induce vomiting. Inhalation: Remove to fresh air, give oxygen if necessary. Skin contact: Flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Eye contact: Flush with water for at least 15 minutes; call physician. For skin contact with molten maleic anhydride, remove solid from skin and treat as normal chemical and thermal burn, and wash with soap and water.
stability: Generally stable. When heated in presence of alkali metals or amines (even in low concentrations of 200 ppm), decomposes rapidly and can overpressurize tanks. Reacts with strong oxidizers. No reactivity except in presence of water (corrosive).
incompatibility: Not corrosive to metals except in the presence of water.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Use protective equipment including goggles, face shield, rubber gloves, rubber boots, coveralls, rubber apron. Use organic vapor-acid gas canister. Dike and let spill solidify, then dispose. Alternative, add water to dissolve spill (forming maleic acid) and neutralize with soda ash, then dispose. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * Hydrolizes slowly with cold water; frothing with hot water. + Unavailable
general_note: Will burn skin and eyes; dangerous to aquatic life.

synonyms: Isobutenyl methyl ketone; Isopropylideneacetone; Methyl iso-butenyl ketone; Methyl isobutenyl ketone; 4-Methyl-3-penten-2-one; iso-Propylideneacetone
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, carbon dioxide or dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Wear complete protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus. Cool exposed tanks with water. Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flammable, dangerous fire risk, vapor forms explosive mixture with air. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Irritation of eyes, headaches, coughing, difficult breathing, nose and throat irritation, mild intoxication.
short_term_exposure: 5 minutes—100 ppm predicted eye and mucous membrane irritation with difficult breathing, headache. Similar exposure at 800 ppm. Predicted severe eye and respiratory irritation. Vapor conc. 500 ppm for 30-60 min. considered dangerous to life.
first_aid: Immediately remove victim from exposure and treat on symptomatic bases. Flush skin promptly with soap and water. If swallowed, do not induce vomiting. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable. Reacts with oxidizing agents; strong alkalis (caustics), and mineral acids.
incompatibility: Non-corrosive to steel.
cargo_group: Group 18 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderately toxic by ingestion, inhalation, and skin absorption.

synonyms: alpha-Methacrylic acid; 2-Methylacrylic acid; 2-Methylpropenic acid; 2-Methylpropenoic acid; Propenoic acid, 2-methylene
appearance: Water-white liquid with a vinegar-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, CO2, dry chemicals or water spray.
special_fire_procedures: High temperatures give off toxic acidic fumes. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus, and full protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate to dangerous when heated to decomposition, emitting toxic fumes.
symptoms: Irritation of eyes, nose and throat; skin may experience a slight burning sensation.
first_aid: Move victim to fresh air, keep warm and quiet. Eyes—flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Skin—flush with water then wash with soap. Ingestion—do not induce vomiting. Call a physician immediately.
stability: Normally stable; however, if stored above 120°F for long periods of time, it can polymerize violently, giving off heat. Reacts with oxidizers.
incompatibility: Corrodes steel, wood, cloth and paint. Glass, 302, 304 and 316 stainless steel are suitable.
hazardous_polymerization: Can polymerize violently if stored above 120°F for long periods.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, aprons, boots and acid goggles. Avoid skin contact and prolonged exposure to vapors. Neutralize spills with soda ash and flush with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Methacrylic acid is normally inhibited with hydroquinone or the methyl ether of hydroquinone.
general_note: Vapors are mildly irritating to the eyes; the liquid is strongly corrosive to the skin and eyes.

synonyms: 2-Cyanopropene; Isopropene cyanide; MAN; 2-Propenenitrile, 2-methyl-
appearance: Clear, colorless liquid; no appreciable odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water fog, alcohol foam, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Wear self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing. Use water to cool exposed containers.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Very flammable; tends to polymerize violently rather than burn. Decomposes to toxic products. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Only moderately irritating to eyes and skin. Inhalation: Weakness, headache, confusion, nausea, vomiting, respiratory paralysis, convulsions.
first_aid: Get medical attention. Inhalation: Remove to fresh air, create artificial airway if needed. Eyes: Flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Skin: Wash with soap and water twice. Medical personnel should wear protective clothing. See Medical Kit Information, Appendix B
stability: Generally stable except when heated. Polymerizes on prolonged exposure to light. Reacts with oxidizers and reducers.
incompatibility: Suitable: Iron
hazardous_polymerization: Polymerizes on prolonged exposure to light.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid all contact, including vapor. Remove all ignition sources. Absorb with clay, earth, sawdust. Dispose by authorized incineration or landfill. Wear gloves, goggles, rubber aprons and boots, self-contained breathing apparatus. Wash clothing before reuse. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * NOTE: Detectable odor and TLV are the same, therefore odor is not a reliable method of detecting hazardous concentrations.
general_note: Very toxic, avoid all contact.

synonyms: Marsh gas; Methyl hydride; Natural gas
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; Water, CO2, or dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Keep burning tank and methane tanks adjacent to it cool with a water spray. Stop flow of gas.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Unless the flow of gas can be stopped, putting out a methane fire will permit the accumulation of an explosive concentration of vapor and subsequent explosion or reflash.
symptoms: Liquid can cause frostbite on skin contact. High gaseous concentrations may cause asphyxiation. No systemic effects, even at 5% concentration in air.
first_aid: Remove to fresh air; if breathing has stopped, apply artificial respiration. If the liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Non-corrosive to steel
spill_or_leak_procedure: Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If methane does not catch fire, it will soon boil off. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Simple asphyxiant. Breathing gas may cause unconsciousness without warning because of lack of oxygen.
extraction_note: Boiling point and freezing point values were not legible in the text layer for this page.

synonyms: 2-[2-(2-Methoxyethoxy)ethoxy]ethanol; Triethylene glycol methyl ether
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Unavailable
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard if exposed to heat.
symptoms: Unavailable
first_aid: Eye contact—flush gently with water. Get medical advice if any discomfort.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: No health hazard under normal conditions of handling.

synonyms: Acetic acid, methyl ester
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, dry chemical, or CO2
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective due to low flash point, but water should be used to keep fire-exposed containers cool. If a leak or spill has not ignited, use water spray to disperse the vapors and to protect men attempting to stop a leak. Water may dilute spills to non-flammable mixtures.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous, when exposed to heat or flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Irritation of respiratory passages, eyes, dizziness, depression, burning of eyes.
first_aid: If the eyes are affected, irrigate continuously with water for at least 15 minutes. Obtain medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Compatible with common materials of construction.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Skin contact with liquid causes defatting and cracking of skin. Vapor irritating.

synonyms: Allene-methyl acetylene mixture; MAPP Gas; Methyl acetylene-allene mixture; Propadiene-methyl acetylene mixture; Propyne-allene mixture
molecular_formula: CH3C=CH, H2C=C=CH2, plus other C-3s and C-4s, saturated and unsaturated.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; Water, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Use water spray to cool burning tank and adjacent MAPP tanks.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: MAPP gas is highly flammable but not shock sensitive. Unless the flow of gas can be stopped, putting out a MAPP gas fire will permit the accumulation of an explosive concentration of vapor, and subsequent explosion or reflash.
symptoms: Contact with MAPP liquid may cause frost-type burns.
short_term_exposure: Toxicity is slight, but high concentrations (6000 ppm) can have an anesthetic effect.
first_aid: Remove to fresh air. Give artificial respiration if breathing stops. If liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention.
stability: This cargo is stabilized.
incompatibility: Alloys containing over 67% copper should not be used.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * Boiling Range: -38 to -20°C; -36 to -4°F. ** Freezing Range: -101 to -137°C; -151 to -214°F.
general_note: The toxicity of MAPP is similar to that of propane and acetylene.

synonyms: Acrylic acid, methyl ester; Methyl propenoate; Methyl 2-propenoate; 2-Propenoic acid methyl ester
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Cool tank with a water spray. Supply fire parties with body and respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Irritating vapors are generated in fires. Ignited by heat, sparks or open flame. Fire may cause violent rupture of tank due to polymerization. Flashback along vapor trail may occur.
symptoms: Watering of eyes, severe burning sensation of throat and nasal passages, coughing and sneezing.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Methyl acrylate will polymerize readily, unless inhibited, evolving considerable amounts of heat. At high temperatures it may polymerize even though inhibited.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
hazardous_polymerization: Polymerizes readily unless inhibited; may polymerize even when inhibited at high temperatures.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor severely irritating. Liquid may cause severe damage from prolonged skin contact.

synonyms: Alcohol C-1; Carbinol; Colonial spirits; Columbian spirits; Methanol; Methyl hydroxide; Pyroxylic spirit; Wood alcohol; Wood spirit
appearance: Colorless liquid; smells like wine or shellac thinner
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Avoid breathing vapors. Provide body and respiratory protection for fire parties. Keep tanks cool with water spray. Water may not be effective unless large quantities are used.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Methyl alcohol is a flammable liquid. At "room" temperature, gives off a vapor which is both toxic and, when mixed with air, explosive within certain limits. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Dizziness, unconsciousness, and sighing respiration.
short_term_exposure: 1000 ppm for 1 hour has caused headache, eye irritation and fatigue.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Give artificial respiration if breathing stops. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing. Flush affected areas gently with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable. Can react vigorously with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Compatible with most materials of construction.
cargo_group: Group 20 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: *NOTE: Odor threshold is not considered adequate warning of potential dangerous vapor concentrations.
general_note: Vapor inhalation dangerous. May be absorbed through skin. Poisonous if swallowed.

synonyms: Aminomethane; Monomethyl amine
appearance: Water white to pale straw color; fishy or ammoniacal odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, water spray, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Wear protective clothing, self-contained breathing apparatus and eye protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Vapor very flammable. When heated, can decompose to toxic nitrogen oxides. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Ingestion: Digestive tract burns. Skin: Irritation, dermatitis, burns. Eyes: Irritation, burns, pulmonary edema. Inhalation: Sneezing, coughing, burning chest pain.
short_term_exposure: As little as 20-100 ppm causes eye, nose, throat irritation. Vapor is so irritating that people do not voluntarily continue hazardous exposure.
first_aid: Get medical attention. Eyes and skin: Flush with water at least 15 minutes. If skin burned, do not cover or apply ointment for first 24 hours. Inhalation: Remove to fresh air with mouth to mouth resuscitation or oxygen if needed. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting. If conscious, drink water.
stability: Stable. Can react with acids and oxidizers.
incompatibility: Suitable: Stainless steel, mild steel, iron. Unsuitable: Aluminum, copper, zinc, magnesium.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact including vapor. Secure ignition sources and dilute with water or use absorbent material. Wear hard hat, safety goggles, face shield, rubber gauntlet gloves, rubber apron, rubber safety shoes or rubber boots, self-contained breathing apparatus, as needed. Do not flush spills into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. Keep from entering waterway. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapors are highly irritating and toxic.

synonyms: 1,3-Dimethylbutyl acetate; sec-Hexyl acetate; MAAc; Methyl iso-butyl carbinol acetate; Methyl iso-butyl carbinyl acetate; Methylisoamyl acetate; 4-Methyl-2-pentanol acetate; 4-Methyl-2-pentyl acetate
appearance: Water white liquid; mild fruity odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area—CO2, dry chemical. Open area—foam, water spray.
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flammable, moderate fire risk.
symptoms: Irritation of respiratory passages, vomiting, dizziness, depression, burning of eyes.
short_term_exposure: Animal tests: No primary skin irritation, traces of eye inflammation; 4 hour exposure inhalation killed 1 out of 6; 8 hours exposure killed 5 of 6.
first_aid: Ingestion—induce vomiting. Inhalation—remove victim to fresh air and administer oxygen if necessary. Eye or skin contact—flush gently with water for 15 minutes. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: No effects on steel; will swell rubber and can dissolve certain coatings.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, protective clothing, face shield. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderately toxic by ingestion and inhalation, can cause skin irritation on prolonged exposure.

synonyms: Isobutyl methyl carbinol; Isobutyl methyl methanol; MAOH; Methyl iso-butyl carbinol; 4-Methyl-2-pentanol; MIBC; MIC
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Provide fire parties with respiratory protection if they must enter spaces to fight the fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Burning of nasal passages and watering of eyes, burning or itching at site of skin contact, dizziness or drowsiness.
short_term_exposure: 2900 ppm cause immediate irritation of the eyes, nose and throat; 2-4 hours, narcosis; 8-10 hours, profound depression and possible death.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Relatively stable.
incompatibility: Most materials of construction are satisfactory.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Essentially an anesthetic with little or no cumulative toxicological properties. Prolonged contact with liquid may produce drying and cracking of the skin.

synonyms: Bromomethane; Embafume; Methane, bromo-; Monobromomethane
flash_point (F): Virtually non-flammable in air; burns in oxygen (O2).
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water spray, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Cool tanks in vicinity of fire with a water spray. Leaking tanks must not be approached unless wearing full body and respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Toxic and irritating gases are generated when exposed to heat or fire. Practically non-flammable. Fire and explosion hazard is slight.
symptoms: Double vision, nausea, dizziness, headache. Severe exposure results in convulsions, muscular tremors, and possibly death.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Administer artificial respiration if unconscious. Oxygen administered by trained personnel is often helpful. Get medical attention immediately.
stability: Forms aluminum alkyls in presence of aluminum. Aluminum alkyls are spontaneously ignitable materials.
incompatibility: Not corrosive to most metals.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Personnel without respiratory protection must be kept upwind of spill. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * NOTE: The effects of inhaling this material may be delayed. Exposure to potentially dangerous vapor concentrations can occur before the product can be detected by smell.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Poisonous by inhalation. Effects may be delayed. Liquid causes burns; may be absorbed by clothing, particularly shoes, to cause delayed burns. Class B poison.

synonyms: Chloromethane; Methane, chloro-
appearance: Colorless gas or liquid; faintly sweet odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; CO2, dry chemical, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Keep tank cool with water spray. Both the vapor of the product and its combustion products are poisonous. Provide firefighters with respiratory protection and full protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: As with a Liquefied Flammable Gas, extinguishing the fire without stopping the gas leakage may increase the danger by permitting the accumulation of an explosive mixture. Ignited by heat, sparks or open flame. Toxic and irritating gases are generated in fires.
symptoms: Dizziness, staggering gait, drowsiness; recovery is slow. Frostbitten areas will be white. Death may result from a single high exposure or repeated moderate exposures.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Apply artificial respiration if breathing stops. If the liquid has spilled onto the person, points of contact may be frostbitten. Protect any frozen areas from mechanical damage. Get medical attention.
stability: Decomposes upon contact with moisture. At high temperatures it may decompose to phosgene, chlorine and carbon monoxide.
incompatibility: When in contact with aluminum, the product which forms may ignite spontaneously in air. Do not use aluminum, aluminum alloys, zinc, die castings, magnesium or magnesium alloys.
hazardous_decomposition_products: Phosgene, chlorine, carbon monoxide (at high temperatures).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. Small spills will vaporize and disperse. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Liquefied Flammable Gases are regulated by 46 CFR Part 38.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Vapor very harmful. Liquid or cold gas may cause skin or eye injury similar to frostbite.
extraction_note: * NOTE: Detectable odor is greater than the TLV. Odor threshold value itself was not legible/present in the text layer.
NOTE: Detectable odor is greater than the TLV. Exposure to potentially dangerous vapor concentrations cn occur before the product can be smelled.

synonyms: 6-Ethyl-2-methyl benzenamine; Ethyl-o-toluidine; Methylethyl aniline
appearance: Clear to amber liquid; mildly pungent odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Wear protective clothing, gloves, and goggles and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Mild hazard, toxic fumes of nitrous oxides and CO2 are given off by high temperatures or combustion.
symptoms: Skin develops blue tinge from lack of oxygen in the blood.
short_term_exposure: Rats subject to 260 ppm for 4 hours produced no symptoms.
first_aid: Flush eyes immediately with water for 15 minutes. Wash skin with water. Remove to fresh air.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Soak up spill with sawdust, sand, or incinerate. Wear protective clothing, goggles, have self-contained breathing apparatus at hand. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Severe eye irritant, nonirritating to the skin.

synonyms: 2-Butanone; Ethyl methyl ketone; MEK
appearance: Colorless liquid with a lacquer thinner odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Water spray may be ineffective on fire. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous fire hazard, when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Irritation in eyes, nose, and throat. Dizziness, headache, nausea and lack of communication.
short_term_exposure: Limited by irritant properties of vapor. 30,000 ppm is intolerable to man because of irritation of eyes and nasal passages; 3000 ppm is intolerable to man for more than just a short period of time.
first_aid: Remove any contaminated clothing promptly and flush skin with copious amounts of water. In case of eye burns, flush with water for ten minutes.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Softens and dissolves many plastics.
cargo_group: Group 18 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor is irritating with moderate narcotic effect when inhaled. Vapor very irritating to eyes. Slight skin irritation on contact.

synonyms: Aldehyde-collidine; Aldehydine; 3-Ethyl-6-methyl pyridine; 5-Ethyl-2-methyl pyridine; 5-Ethyl-2-picoline; MEP
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, carbon dioxide, dry chemical, water spray
special_fire_procedures: Wear protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame. Irritating vapors are generated when heated.
symptoms: Redness and swelling from skin contact with liquid.
short_term_exposure: 1700 ppm lethal to a rat in 3.7 hours.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected area with water for 15 minutes. A physician must see all cases of eye contact immediately after eye wash is completed.
stability: Stable. Can react with oxidizing or strongly alkaline (caustic) materials.
incompatibility: Polyethylene-lined containers suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. Keep unprotected personnel away from spill area. Collect material in plastic containers using absorbents, for small spills; flush large spills. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
extraction_note: Health Hazard Ratings printed as '2.22' without comma delimiters in source; interpreted as '2,2,2'.

synonyms: Formic acid, methyl ester; Methyl methanoate
fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, alcohol foam, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Water may not be effective. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus, rubber gloves.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Toxic vapors are generated. Very dangerous when exposed to heat, flame or oxidizers. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Irritation of mucous membranes, narcosis, temporary visual disturbances. Liquid causes skin and eye irritation.
first_aid: Inhalation—move to fresh air, give artificial respiration or oxygen as necessary. Eyes—flush with water for 15 minutes. Skin—wash with soap and water. Ingestion—Do not induce vomiting. Get medical help.
stability: Stable. Slow non-hazardous reaction with water to form formic acid and methyl alcohol. Reacts with oxidizers.
incompatibility: Stainless steel, aluminum or lined carbon steel are suitable.
hazardous_decomposition_products: Formic acid, methyl alcohol (on slow hydrolysis).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Secure ignition sources. Restrict access. Disperse and flush. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus, rubber gloves, goggles or safety glasses. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor and liquid are irritating to eyes, nose, skin and throat.

synonyms: Hexone; isobutyl methyl ketone; Isopropylacetone; 4-Methyl-2-pentanone; MIBK; MIK
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Fire parties must wear respiratory protection. Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Irritating vapors are generated when heated. Dangerous fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame; moderate explosion hazard when vapor exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Headache, dizziness and nausea.
short_term_exposure: 200-400 ppm for 5 minutes has produced eye irritation; 400 ppm for 5 minutes may produce nasal irritation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. If swallowed, do not induce vomiting. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Will soften many plastics.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor causes eye, nose, throat irritation. Aspirated methyl isobutyl ketone may cause severe lung damage and present a significant hazard. Repeated or prolonged skin contact may cause defatting of the skin with primary irritation resulting.

synonyms: Crystalite; Methacrylate monomer; Methacrylic acid, methyl ester; Methyl methacrylate monomer, inh.; Methyl alpha-methacrylate; Methyl-2-methyl propenoate; 2-Methylpropenoic acid; 2-Propenoic acid, 2-methyl-, methyl ester
fire_extinguishing_agent: Foam, carbon dioxide and dry chemicals
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water. Wear eye protection, self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Ignited by heat, sparks, or open flame. Fire may cause violent rupture of tank because of polymerization.
symptoms: Smarting of the skin and first-degree burns on short exposure and may cause second-degree burns on long exposure.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Polymerizes readily. Methyl methacrylate will not decompose on prolonged storage if properly inhibited.
incompatibility: Noncorrosive to steel, aluminum or stainless steel.
hazardous_polymerization: Polymerizes readily; will not decompose on prolonged storage if properly inhibited.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor irritating.

synonyms: AMS; Isopropenylbenzene; 1-Methyl-1-phenylethylene; Phenylpropylene
appearance: Clear yellow liquid; characteristic aromatic odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, foam, CO2, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Will cause skin irritation if not removed promptly. Breathing considerable quantities may cause headache and/or dizziness.
first_aid: Skin contact—flush body splashes with plenty of water. Inhalation—remove victim to fresh air. Administer artificial respiration if necessary.
stability: Stable. Can react with oxidizing materials
incompatibility: May cause rubber to swell.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield and protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure all sources of ignition. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Avoid skin contact. Not known to be absorbed.

synonyms: tert-Butyl methyl ether; MTBE
appearance: Clear, colorless liquid; sharp, terpene-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, dry chemical, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water spray.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flammable and, when confined, explosive. Flashback along vapor trail may occur.
symptoms: Irritates eyes, skin, mucous membranes. Inhalation: For prolonged exposure, coughing, shortness of breath, dizziness, intoxication. For short exposure, dizziness.
first_aid: Inhalation: Remove to fresh air, give oxygen or artificial respiration as needed. Eyes: Flush with water for at least 15 minutes, hold eyelids open, call physician. Skin: Wash with water. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting.
stability: Generally stable. Forms peroxides at much slower rate than most ethers. Reacts with mineral acids, organic acids, other oxidizers.
incompatibility: Compatible with steel, iron, aluminum, copper, magnesium, zinc, neoprene, polyethylene, polypropylene. Incompatible with viton elastomer.
cargo_group: Group 41 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Stop release, remove all ignition sources. Dyke to prevent spill from entering sewers (explosion hazard, pollution) and waterways. Remove spill with inert absorbent. Wear goggles or face shield, boots, and use self-contained breathing apparatus if spill large or in confined area. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Not too toxic, similar to gasoline.

synonyms: Ligroin (in U.S.A.); Naphtha; Petroleum spirits; Turpentine substitute
appearance: Water white liquid with gasoline-like odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Foam, carbon dioxide, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Do not use straight hose water stream.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Inhalation: Mild irritation of respiratory tract. Severe lung irritant. Central nervous system excitement followed by depression.
first_aid: Inhalation: Remove victim to fresh air. Administer artificial respiration if necessary. Ingestion: DO NOT induce vomiting. Eyes: Wash with copious amounts of water.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear polyethylene gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.

synonyms: Treacle
molecular_formula: A mixture of sucrose and sugars
fire_extinguishing_agent: Non-flammable
special_fire_procedures: Non-flammable
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Non-flammable and non-combustible.
symptoms: Non-toxic
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and flush affected areas gently with water.
stability: Stable. Reacts with conc. nitric acid and conc. sulphuric acid. Ferments when diluted with salt or fresh water.
incompatibility: Mild steel and stainless steel are suitable.
hazardous_decomposition_products: Carbon dioxide, ethanol/higher alcohol vapor (during fermentation).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wash area with water after removing bulk of spill by general means. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * Unregulated, Table 2, 46 CFR Part 153. ** 120 vapor only + Unassigned
general_note: Non-toxic. Molasses fermentation occurs when molasses is diluted with salt or fresh water and is accelerated by heat. During fermentation CO2 (with possible traces of ethanol and higher alcohol vapor) is given off, which will produce inhalation hazard in compartment containing molasses residue.

synonyms: Diethylene imidoxide; Diethylene oximide; Diethylenimide oxide; Tetrahydro-1,4-oxazine; Tetrahydro-2H-1,4-oxazine; Tetrahydro-p-oxazine
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, water fog, alcohol foam
special_fire_procedures: Provide fire parties with full body and respiratory protection.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to flame or heat. When heated to decomposition, it emits highly toxic fumes of oxides of nitrogen.
symptoms: Burning of throat and eyes; itching or burning of the skin at site of contact.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: This material is more stable than most of the other amines listed in this volume. It is a mild base.
incompatibility: Copper and its alloys and galvanized iron are not compatible.
cargo_group: Group 7 of compatibility chart. See also Appendix I—Exceptions to the Chart.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear butyl rubber gloves, plastic protective apron, self-contained breathing apparatus. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Small spills may be washed away with water. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor moderately irritating. Liquid causes severe burns.

chemical_name: MOTOR FUEL ANTI-KNOCK COMPOUNDS (containing lead alkyls)
synonyms: Lead tetraethyl; Lead tetramethyl; TEL; Tetraethyl lead compounds; Tetramethyl lead compounds; TML
appearance: Oily liquid; containing dye; musty sweet odor
fire_grade: D or E: Combustible liquid, depending upon flash point.
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Tanks exposed to fire should be kept cool with a water spray to prevent decomposition of the lead compounds. Because of the high toxicity of the compound and its combustion products, only personnel with full respiratory protection should approach burning antiknock compounds. ALL OTHERS SHOULD BE EVACUATED AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE!
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame. Dangerous. When heated to decomposition, it emits highly toxic fumes of lead.
symptoms: Nervousness, irritability, insomnia, dreaming; emotional instability; hallucinations, anorexia, vomiting, constipation, pallor and tremor.
first_aid: Personnel MUST avoid inhaling the vapors or allowing the liquid to touch the skin. Clothing and other absorbent material in contact with the liquid should be destroyed since they cannot be decontaminated. Liquid spilled onto the skin should be scrubbed off with kerosene at once. Get medical attention.
stability: Relatively stable at ambient temperatures, but it may decompose if heated above 212°F.
incompatibility: May be carried in steel tanks. No chemical effect on common materials but will readily permeate absorbent materials. Avoid contact with oxidizing agents or concentrated acids.
cargo_group: Unassigned in compatibility chart. For compatibility assistance, call G-MTH-1 (202-267-1577).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, full protective clothing, eye protection and self-contained breathing apparatus. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * TLV/TWA (ppm)—0.1 to 0.13 mg/m3 as lead. + Unavailable
general_note: Prolonged skin contact, ingestion or inhalation of high vapor may result in a toxic psychosis causing anxiety which may progress to mania and death. Class B poison.

synonyms: Drycleaners naphtha; Drycleaners safety solvent; Ligroin (in U.S.A.); Mineral spirits; Petroleum solvent; Spotting solvent; Stoddard solvent; White spirits
fire_extinguishing_agent: Foam, dry chemical or CO2
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flammable, moderate fire risk.
symptoms: Inhalation—intoxication may result from high vapor concentration.
first_aid: Inhalation: Remove victim to fresh air. Administer artificial respiration if necessary. Ingestion: DO NOT induce vomiting. Eyes: Flush with water for 15 minutes. Call a doctor.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Solvent effects on some paints and rubber. Carbon steel satisfactory.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Toxic. Prolonged or repeated skin contact may cause defatting of the skin and may produce dermatitis from daily contact.

synonyms: Light naphtha; Ligroin (in U.S.A.); Naphtha, petroleum; Painters naphtha; Petroleum solvent; Refined solvent naphtha; Solvent naphtha; Varnish makers' & painters' naphtha
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area—CO2, dry chemical. Open area—foam.
special_fire_procedures: Fight like gasoline fire. Wear respiratory devices.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Flammable, moderate fire risk. Produces suffocating atmosphere of smoke, CO2, and fumes
symptoms: Headache, dizziness, insomnia, coughing, diarrhea, bronchitis and pneumonia, nervousness and irritability.
short_term_exposure: 4000 to 7000 ppm for 1 hour results in development of symptoms of narcosis.
first_aid: Inhalation: Immediately remove victim from contaminated area. Get medical attention. If splashed in eyes, wash thoroughly.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Solvent effects on some paints and rubbers. Carbon steel not affected. Corrosive in presence of salt water.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus. Secure all ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Will remove oils from skin. Prolonged contact with liquid may produce drying and cracking of the skin, and may produce dermatitis from daily contact. Toxicity by absorption, inhalation, ingestion.

synonyms: Camphor tar; Naphthaline; Naphthene; Tar camphor; White tar
appearance: Colorless liquid or white solid; odor of mothballs
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Do not direct a hose into a tank of molten naphthalene. Otherwise the naphthalene will be spattered about with explosive force. Water or foam must be applied carefully to molten naphthalene to prevent excessive frothing. Wear eye protection, self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Combustible Grade E solid normally carried in the molten state. When carried molten, it presents a fire hazard comparable to that of a Grade C flammable liquid. Naphthalene vapor or dust can form explosive mixtures with air. Toxic vapors given off in a fire.
symptoms: Eye irritation, headache, nausea, profuse perspiration, vomiting.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention. * NOTE: Detectable odor is greater than the TLV. Exposure to potentially dangerous vapor concentrations can occur before the product can be smelled.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Noncorrosive. Most materials of construction are satisfactory.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Upon spilling, the material will solidify and can be scraped up with nonsparking shovels into a waste container. Naphthalene spilling into water will either solidify and sink, or solidify into a foam and float. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Normally transported at elevated temperatures. See 46 CFR 36—Elevated Temperature Cargoes.
general_note: Molten liquid is scalding on contact. Vapor is irritating to skin and eyes.

synonyms: No common synonyms.
appearance: Gold to dark red to black liquid; penetrating, persistent, putrid odor

general_note: Breathing of vapors is extremely dangerous. Little warning of danger is at first apparent and initial symptoms are obscure. Liquid burns the skin forming deep ulcers which leave leathery scars.

general_note: No hazard for gas. Liquid can cause severe "burns" and tissue damage on contact with skin.

fire_extinguishing_agent: Foam, dry chemical, carbon dioxide
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire. Cool exposed tanks with water. Use water spray to "knock down" vapors.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Highly dangerous when exposed to heat or flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Low toxicity. Very high concentration of vapors may cause narcosis.
first_aid: Vapor inhalation—move victim to fresh air. If breathing stops, administer artificial respiration. Liquid—have victim drink plenty of water or milk. DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING. Call a doctor.
stability: Stable. Dangerous reaction possible with oxidizing agents. Keep away from heat, sparks, or open flame.
incompatibility: Mild steel and stainless steel are suitable. Natural rubber will soften and deteriorate rapidly.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear polyethylene gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all purpose canister mask available. For gas leaks keep vapor concentration below explosive mixture range. Secure ignition sources. Do not flush spill into confined spaces where flammable vapors can accumulate. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapors may cause dizziness or difficult breathing. Liquid is harmful if swallowed.

synonyms: Ethene, tetrachloro-; Ethylene tetrachloride; Perchlorethylene; Tetrachlorethene; Tetrachlorethylene; Tetrachloroethylene
fire_extinguishing_agent: none
special_fire_procedures: In case of fire near a perchloroethylene tank, cool the tank with water. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Does not burn. The liquid or vapor in contact with a hot surface or a flame can decompose to form phosgene, which is highly toxic.
symptoms: Headache, dizziness, blurred vision, tears, burning of the eyes, irritation of nose and throat.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Stable up to 258°F; at this temperature the product decomposes and gives off poisonous fumes.
incompatibility: Compatible with galvanized iron, black iron or steel.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Prolonged, excessive, or repeated exposures to the product in any form are hazardous. Can defat the skin and may produce dermatitis from frequent daily contact.

synonyms: Paraffin jelly; Petrolatum jelly; Petroleum jelly; Vaseline; Yellow petrolatum
molecular_formula: Mixture of liquid or semi-liquid aliphatic hydrocarbons
appearance: Colorless to amber, oily translucent; no odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area—CO2, dry chemical. Open area—water spray, foam.
special_fire_procedures: Water or foam may cause frothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Non-toxic
first_aid: Liquid on skin—remove contaminated clothing and cool affected areas with cold water. Liquid in eye—flood eyes gently with clean sea or fresh water. Continue washing for at least 15 minutes. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with hot liquid. Wear goggles or face shield, protective clothing for hot liquids. Wash away with water. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Normally transported at elevated temperatures. See 46 CFR 36—Elevated Temperature Cargoes. † Unassigned
general_note: Non-toxic, but possibility of thermal burns from hot liquid.

synonyms: Benzene, hydroxy-; Carbolic acid; Hydroxybenzene; Monohydroxybenzene; Oxybenzene; Phenic acid; Phenyl hydroxide; Phenylic acid
appearance: Colorless-to-pink solid or thick liquid; sweet, disinfectant-like odor (like Lysol)
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Where there is danger of skin contact, provide full body protection. Full respiratory protection should be worn by fire parties at all times.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: When heated, it emits toxic and irritating fumes. Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Headache, weakness, ringing of the ears, and irregular breathing. Skin contact will cause white, wrinkled, soft skin at site of contact. Absorption through skin is rapid and can cause death within 30 minutes after exposure.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get victim to a hospital or treatment center as soon as possible. All exposure victims should get medical attention.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Rubber, aluminum and its alloys, zinc and lead are attacked by phenol.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Do not permit anyone near spill unless suitably protected. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Normally transported at elevated temperatures. See 46 CFR 36—Elevated Temperature Cargoes. * Vapor Pressure: 30.6 mmHg at 25°C.
general_note: Causes severe burns. Poisonous by skin absorption. Class B poison.
extraction_note: Solid' UN number printed unclearly in source; noted as 1671 based on standard phenol solid UN number pattern in this reference — flagged for visual confirmation.

synonyms: Metaphosphoric acid; Orthophosphoric acid; meta-Phosphoric acid; ortho-Phosphoric acid; White phosphoric acid
electrical_group: B (based upon possible hydrogen gas (H2) generation should a leak or spill occur)
fire_extinguishing_agent: Non-flammable
special_fire_procedures: Keep tank cool with water spray. Since toxic fumes of oxides of phosphorous are evolved when phosphoric acid is heated to decomposition, fire fighters should be provided with self-contained breathing apparatus.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Phosphoric acid will not burn. It will react with many metals, giving off hydrogen gas which is highly flammable. If hydrogen is trapped in a confined space, it can form an explosive mixture with air. See data sheet for hydrogen.
symptoms: Irritation of skin in contact with liquid; burning of eyes.
first_aid: Skin contact—remove contaminated clothing and flush affected areas gently with large amounts of water. Eye contact—immediately flush eyes gently with water; continue to flush for 15 minutes. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable over a wide temperature range.
incompatibility: Very corrosive to ordinary ferrous metals and alloys particularly at temperatures above 180°F.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, protective clothing. Have body shield available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. Flush spills with large amounts of water or, if possible, cover contaminated surface and spill with sodium bicarbonate, or a soda ash-slaked lime mixture (50-50). Mix and add water, if necessary to form a slurry. Scoop up slurry. Wash site with soda ash solution. In the event of a major spill, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: The information provided is for 100% phosphoric acid.
general_note: Causes burns.

synonyms: White phosphorus; WP; Yellow phosphorus
fire_extinguishing_agent: EXCLUDE AIR; use water spray, sand, or earth
special_fire_procedures: Use suitable respiratory protection. DO NOT use high-pressure water stream, as it may spread molten phosphorus over a wider area. Do not use carbon dioxide extinguisher. Try to smother fire with sand. Wear full protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Pyrophoric—ignites spontaneously when exposed to air and burns vigorously. When shipped in bulk, air is kept away by a water blanket. Burning releases dense irritating fumes; intense white smoke is formed.
symptoms: Weakness and unusual sensitivity of eyes to light. Vapor of burning phosphorus is irritating to nose, throat and lungs. Skin contact causes burns and ulcers.
first_aid: Skin contact—immediately plunge infected area into water or get victim under a flood-type shower and deluge contacted parts. Large amounts of copper sulfate solution (10-15%) should be applied. Continue this for 3 minutes and then try to wash away the phosphorus particles. Contact a doctor.
stability: Phosphorus must be shipped covered with water, because on exposure to air it ignites spontaneously. Reacts vigorously with oxidizing agents. Incompatible with dry air.
cargo_group: Unassigned in compatibility chart. For compatibility assistance, call G-MTH-1 (202-267-1577).
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, protective clothing, large face shield. Avoid contact with the spilled material. Cover with wet sand. Spray with water to keep sand wet. Scoop into buckets or barrel of water. After standing overnight, recover and repackage. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Causes severe burns. Vapor inhalation is very dangerous. Can be absorbed through the skin.

synonyms: 1,2-Benzenedicarboxylic acid anhydride; 1,3-Dioxophalan; 1,3-Isobenzofurandione; PAN; Phthalandione; Phthalic acid anhydride
appearance: White or colorless crystals with a mild odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water fog, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Water stream may cause frothing. Steam is an effective extinguishing agent for fighting molten phthalic anhydride fires in tanks.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Molten phthalic anhydride will burn if ignited and its vapor may form an explosive mixture with air.
symptoms: Coughing, sneezing, burning sensations in nose and throat, increased mucous secretion; on contact, phthalic anhydride is very irritating to wet skin.
short_term_exposure: 25 mg/m3 in air produced some signs of mucous membrane irritation with 30 mg/m3 causing definite eye irritation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; spraying or gargling with water will help relieve nasal or throat irritations; if respiratory distress or violent coughing occurs, administration of oxygen is helpful; call a physician immediately. Skin contact—wash affected area thoroughly with soap and water; remove contaminated clothing and launder before reuse. Eye contact—flush eyes thoroughly with water and irrigate for 15 minutes or more. Call a physician.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Compatible with most materials when dry; however, when wet, phthalic anhydride forms a solution of phthalic acid which attacks ordinary iron and mild steel.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Body shield and self-contained breathing apparatus should be available. If possible, cover spill with soda ash or sodium bicarbonate. Mix, and add water if necessary to effect good mixing. Scoop up slurry and wash site with soda ash solution. Secure all ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: Normally transported at elevated temperatures. See 46 CFR 36—Elevated Temperature Cargoes.
general_note: Local irritant to body tissues, especially moist skin. Vapor irritating to skin, eyes, nose, throat and upper respiratory tract. Molten material causes severe burns.

synonyms: Butene resins; Polybutylene; Polyisobutene; Polyisobutylene, plastics, resins & waxes
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical or foam
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Mild fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Non-toxic
first_aid: Remove to fresh air, apply artificial respiration if needed.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield and protective clothing. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Non-toxic. Vapor may act as a simple asphyxiant in high concentration.

synonyms: PAPI
appearance: Dark brown liquid; no appreciable odor.
fire_extinguishing_agent: Confined area-CO2; self-extinguishing.
special_fire_procedures: Wear protective clothing and respiratory protection. Self-extinguishing. Reacts withwatr to evolve CO, and form solid polymer.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Irritating vapors given off when heated. Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame; can react with oxidizing materials.
symptoms: labored breathing, watering of eyes
short_term_exposure: animal tests showed inhalation off2.2 2.2 ppm were fatal to 4 ofo 6 rats. No toxic effects were observed on skin contact; eye distress was temporary. LD50 was 10,000 mg/kg
first_aid: -Remove victim to frsh air;administer to oxygenif breathing is labored. Flush skin with atningwater after removing contaminated clothing. Wash eye with water for at least 15 minutes. Ingestion-inducevomiting 3 times, follow with quart of milk and a mild cathartic. Get medical help.
stability: stable. Heat, water, and acids will react to evolve CO₂
incompatibility: ot corrosive to mild steel, however, aluminum cannot be used.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Cover spill with water spray. Cleanup. Secure all ignition sources. Wear protective clothing and possibly respiratory protection.
remarks: : Storing under a dry inert atmosphere at slight positive pressure to eliminate traces of moisture contamination is imperative. † Unavailable Unassigned
general_note: Single short exposure to skin may cause considerable irritation. Liquid expected to burn eyes. Inhalation causes very slight respiratory irritation.

synonyms: Dimethylmethane; Propyl hydride
appearance: Colorless gas or liquid; natural-gas odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Stop flow of gas; CO2, dry chemical, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Tanks exposed to fire should be kept cool with a continuous spray of water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Unless the flow of gas can be stopped, extinguishing a propane fire will permit the accumulation of an explosive concentration of vapor, and subsequent explosion or reflash.
symptoms: Headache, dizziness, drowsiness. Contact with the liquid will cause frostbite.
short_term_exposure: A vapor concentration of 10,000 ppm for brief periods has been reported as producing no symptoms.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Give artificial respiration if breathing stops. Get medical attention. If liquid has spilled onto the skin, points of contact may be frostbitten; handle gently and protect from mechanical damage. DO NOT RUB. Get medical attention. *NOTE: Exposure to potentially dangerous vapor concentrations can occur before the product can be detected by smell.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Usual materials of construction are suitable.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Secure all possible sources of ignition and call the fire department. The spilled liquid will boil away rapidly, leaving no residue. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid causes frostbite on skin contact. Cold vapor causes skin damage. Inhalation can lead to asphyxiation.

synonyms: 1-Amino-2-propanol; 2-Hydroxypropylamine; Isopropanolamine; MIPA; Monoisopropanolamine
fire_extinguishing_agent: Dry chemical, water spray, alcohol foam, or carbon dioxide
special_fire_procedures: Wear goggles, self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Irritating vapors given off when heated. Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame; can react with oxidizing materials.
symptoms: Nose and throat irritation.
first_aid: In case of skin contact, wash well with soap and water. For eye contact, wash with large amounts of water.
stability: Stable; forms soaps with organic acids.
incompatibility: Will remove paint, swells rubber; recommend type 304 stainless steel clad tanks.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Avoid contact with liquid. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Single short exposure to skin may cause considerable irritation. Liquid expected to burn eyes. Inhalation causes very slight respiratory irritation.
extraction_note: This page's fire hazard and health hazard data blocks in the source text layer duplicate the content of the preceding entry (Polymethylene Polyphenyl Isocyanate) — extracted as printed rather than corrected; recommend visual re-check of PDF page 247.

synonyms: 3-Amino-1-propanol; 3-Hydroxypropylamine; 3-Propanolamine; 1-Propanol, 3-amino-
appearance: Light yellow to colorless liquid; fishy odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, dry powder, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame.
symptoms: Irritation of mucous membranes and respiratory tract. Severe exposure results in blisters and burns.
first_aid: Remove victim to fresh air. Give artificial respiration or oxygen as necessary. Flush eyes and skin well with water. Remove contaminated clothing. Wash out mouth with water if ingested.
stability: Stable.
incompatibility: Copper and copper alloys are readily corroded.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear self-contained breathing apparatus and rubber gloves. Absorb material on vermiculite, sweep up, mix with dry caustic, wrap in paper and burn in an incinerator. Wash spill site. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Moderately irritating to skin and eyes.
extraction_note: Health Hazard Ratings printed as '11,41' in source text; interpreted as '1,1,1' but flagged for visual confirmation.

synonyms: Hydracrylic acid, beta-lactone; 2-Oxetanone; Propanolide; beta-Propionolactone
fire_extinguishing_agent: Water, dry chemical, foam, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Wear self-contained breathing apparatus, full protective clothing, rubber gloves to prevent all contact with liquid. Cool exposed tanks with water.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Combustible; containers may explode in fire. Vapors of unburned material are very toxic.
symptoms: Inhalation—irritation of nose, throat and respiratory tract. Liquid causes eye irritation and tears. Skin contact results in irritation and blistering. Ingestion—mouth and stomach burns.
first_aid: Inhalation—move victim to fresh air. Give artificial respiration or oxygen as necessary. Eyes—flush with water for 15 minutes. Skin—flush with water. Fluid from blisters will cause additional blisters. Ingestion—give large amounts of water, induce vomiting.
stability: Stable but at elevated temperatures can polymerize.
hazardous_polymerization: Can polymerize at elevated temperatures.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear full protective clothing. Avoid any contact whatsoever. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus and rubber gloves. Disperse and flush large spills. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * Bulk shipment not permitted. + Unavailable + Unassigned
general_note: Suspected carcinogen. Vapor moderately irritating. Liquid is a fairly severe skin irritant. Poison. Get medical attention after all exposures to this compound.
extraction_note: Source page carries a note: 'THIS CARGO IS CURRENTLY NOT PERMITTED TO BE SHIPPED IN BULK IN U.S. WATERS.'
NOTE: This cargo is currently not permitted to be shipped in bulk in U.S. waters)

synonyms: Methyl acetaldehyde; Propanal; Propionic aldehyde; Propyl aldehyde; Propylic aldehyde
appearance: Colorless liquid with suffocating and fruity odor
fire_extinguishing_agent: Carbon dioxide, dry chemical and alcohol foam.
special_fire_procedures: Keep tanks cool with water spray. Provide fire fighters with self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing. Fire may be difficult to control due to ease with which vapor is re-ignited. Water may be ineffective on fire.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Extreme fire hazard due to low flash point. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area. Reacts vigorously with oxidizers.
symptoms: Dizziness, drowsiness.
first_aid: Skin contact should be thoroughly washed off with soap and water. In case of liquid contact of the eyes, flush eyes with water for at least 15 minutes then obtain medical treatment.
stability: Highly reactive. Normally stored under nitrogen blanket. Reacts vigorously with oxidizers.
incompatibility: Either stainless steel or aluminum are suitable materials. Tanks may be coated with phenolic resin.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, self-contained breathing apparatus, protective clothing. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If possible, cover with sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3). Add small amount of water and mix. Scoop up. Wash site with soap solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Liquid irritating to skin and causes eye injury. Vapor inhalation dangerous.

synonyms: Ethane carboxylic acid; Ethylformic acid; Methacetonic acid; Methylacetic acid; Propanoic acid
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, water spray, CO2, dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: Provide fire fighters with goggles, self-contained breathing apparatus and protective clothing.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Ignited by heat and open flame.
symptoms: Causes burns on the skin, particularly mucous membranes (mouth, nose) and eyes.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical attention.
stability: Stable. When heated, emits acrid fumes.
incompatibility: Corrosive.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Body shield and self-contained breathing apparatus should be available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If possible, cover spill with soda ash or sodium bicarbonate. Mix and add water if necessary to effect good mixing, scoop up slurry and wash site with soda ash solution. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapor extremely irritating. Liquid causes severe burns.

synonyms: Methylacetic anhydride; Propanoic acid anhydride; Propanoic anhydride; Propionyl oxide
fire_extinguishing_agent: Carbon dioxide or dry chemical
special_fire_procedures: DO NOT USE WATER as extinguishing media; propionic anhydride reacts slowly with water to form propionic acid—reaction rate increases with temperature.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Moderate fire hazard when exposed to heat or flame; more of a health hazard than a fire or stability hazard.
symptoms: Respiratory irritation, skin irritation.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; apply artificial respiration if breathing stops. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water. Get medical attention if discomfort persists.
stability: Decomposes on contact with water. Can react with oxidizing materials.
incompatibility: Noncorrosive to aluminum or stainless steel.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Have self-contained breathing apparatus available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
remarks: * Reacts with water to form propionic acid.
general_note: Vapors irritating when inhaled. Liquid irritating to skin on contact. May produce sensitization effects.

synonyms: Cyanoethane; Ether cyanatus; Ethyl cyanide; Hydrocyanic ether; Propanenitrile; Propionic nitrile
fire_extinguishing_agent: Alcohol foam, dry chemical, CO2
special_fire_procedures: Cool exposed tanks with water. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus and full protective clothing including boots.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Produces toxic gases of hydrogen cyanide, nitrogen oxides, and carbon monoxide when heated or near open flame.
symptoms: Dizziness, nausea, rapid pulse, respiratory distress, cyanosis, coma. May be fatal if inhaled, swallowed or absorbed through skin.
short_term_exposure: LD50 for rats in a 4 hour period was less than 1.6 gm/l.
first_aid: Antidote is amyl nitrite. Always have a cyanide kit at hand. Remove to fresh air. Administer artificial respiration or oxygen as necessary. See Medical Kit Information, Appendix B
stability: Stable. Incompatible with strong acids and alkalies.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Keep people away. Secure sources of ignition. Shut off leak if without risk. Stay upwind. Wear self-contained breathing apparatus and full protective clothing including boots. For large spills, dike and pump into salvage tanks. Use water spray to knock down vapors. Prevent run off to sewers. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: May be fatal if absorbed through skin. Liquid causes burns.

synonyms: Acetic acid, isopropyl ester; Isopropyl acetate; Isopropyl ester of acetic acid; 2-Propyl acetate; sec-Propyl acetate
fire_extinguishing_agent: CO2, dry chemical, alcohol foam, water fog
special_fire_procedures: Use of dry chemical where it can get into a tank of isopropyl acetate is not recommended. Fires involving spills outside of tanks can be extinguished with dry chemical.
unusual_fire_explosion_hazards: Dangerous. Keep away from heat and open flame. Flashback along vapor trail may occur. Vapor may explode if ignited in an enclosed area.
symptoms: Dizziness and drowsiness.
first_aid: Vapor—remove victim to fresh air; if breathing stops, apply artificial respiration. Skin or eye contact—remove contaminated clothing and gently flush affected areas with water for 15 minutes. Get medical advice or attention.
stability: Hydrolyzes (reacts with water) on standing to form acetic acid and isopropyl alcohol. The presence of bases (alkalis) speeds up the reaction. Reacts vigorously with oxidizing agents.
incompatibility: Softens or dissolves many plastics.
spill_or_leak_procedure: Wear rubber gloves, face shield, protective clothing. Have all-purpose canister mask available. Avoid contact with liquid. Secure ignition sources. If a spill occurs, call the National Response Center, 800-424-8802.
general_note: Vapors harmful.
extraction_note: Health Hazard Ratings printed as 'A, A, e' (illegible) in source text; interpreted as '1,1,1' based on the surrounding numeric pattern, but flagged for visual confirmation.
